jobs.description:
Doctoral student position – Evaluating novel mineral sources for treatment of micronutrient deficiencies in humans

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

The ETH Zurich Laboratory of Epigenetics, Nutrition and Metabolism and Sustainable Food Processing Group in the Department of Health Science and Technology are running a joint strategic research line on Microalgae and plant-based foods in Human Nutrition and Health . The Sustainable Food Processing group focuses on a system-oriented approach in food production via the consideration of the total value chain, including emerging needs in society and their environmental, economic, and social impact. Innovative raw materials are utilized within urban farming and processing concepts to enable new ways of sustainable food supply. The Laboratory of Epigenetics, Nutrition and Metabolism aims to gain insights into the complex relationship between nutrition, metabolism and the epigenome with advanced techniques such as single-cell and next-generation sequencing techniques as well as human and murine in vivo and in vitro studies and combine these with genome-wide computational and bioinformatic analysis. With strong support from these two ETH groups, we are recruiting as soon as possible a talented and highly motivated doctoral student on the topic of ‘Novel sources of minerals for treatment of micronutrient deficiencies in humans’, focusing on investigating the absorption and bioavailability of novel mineral sources in vivo in clinical trials.

Project background

Micronutrient deficiency is a widespread global health problem, primarily driven by inadequate dietary intake. More than 5 billion people are estimated to not consume enough of at least one micronutrient. Among those, mineral deficiencies can be particularly critical, namely, iron, calcium, zinc, and magnesium deficiencies, which are particularly common in low- and middle-income countries due to low-mineral diets and primarily affect women and children.

Dietary minerals are typically obtained from a variety of foods including animal-based products such as meat, dairy, and seafood, and plant-based foods such as legumes, cereals, nuts, seeds, and leafy vegetables. However, reliance on conventional animal-based foods raises concerns related to environmental sustainability, ethical considerations, and dietary preferences. Although plant-based foods are generally more sustainable, they often have lower mineral content, bioaccessibility, as well as bioavailability due to the presence of absorption inhibitors such as phytates and polyphenols. Given these limitations, the need exists to explore alternative, more sustainable, and mineral-dense food sources that can effectively address global mineral deficiencies.

Novel mineral sources, such as microalgae, could be a rich source of essential minerals, including iron, calcium, zinc, and magnesium, along with proteins, lipids, vitamins, and other bioactive compounds. However, the bioavailability of these minerals needs to be assessed with in vivo clinical trials before large scale application in humans.

Job description

As a doctoral student, you will be responsible for research working towards exploring the absorption and bioavailability of novel mineral sources with clinical trials.
• Summarize the existing knowledge on minerals from novel sources for human nutrition and health
• Design intervention meals (including sensory test) for clinical trials
• Assess the bioaccessibility of minerals in vitro
• Evaluate the mineral bioavailability in vitro
• Carry out clinical trials related to human nutrition enriched with novel mineral sources (key)
• Support teaching activities and co-supervise MSc and BSc students
• Act at the interface between science and technology when supervising students and collaborating with partners from academia and industry
• Support grant applications for the team and support related activities from Singapore-ETH Centre, Bezos Centre for Sustainable Protein at NUS, ETH World Food System Center WFSC, and ETH for Development ETH4D competence center

Profile
• A MSc in Nutrition and Health, Clinical Trials, Food Science and Technology (with strong nutrition or clinical experience), or relevant fields
• A strong passion for nutrition and health, sustainability, and novel food sources
• Expertise and interest in working with human/clinical related works (GCP certificate is compulsory, however, can be obtained after starting)
• Experience and strong interest in nutrition assessment using in vivo models
• Ability to work in a dynamic, international, and interdisciplinary team
• Ability to collaborate with different teams and national and international partners
• Interest in working independently and supervising students
• Strong verbal and written communication skills in English
• Scientific curiosity and motivation to perform scientifically rigorous experimental work

We offer

You will be working with a leading research team on Microalgae and Plant-based Foods in Human Nutrition and Health with strong support from both ETH groups. You will be working with state-of-the-art research equipment in an excellent and open working environment. ETH Zurich and the team provide excellent training opportunities for career development and strong networks in both sustainable food and nutrition. The project will also get support from research assistants when needed.

Living expenses will be supported with a fixed-rate standard monthly doctoral student salary according to ETH guidelines .

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. The position is open to international students. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered. The call is open until we identify a suitable candidate. There is no clear deadline for applications. The latest starting date is expected to be 01 September 2026, the earlier the better.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents (In English, PDF format):
• Motivation letter (max. 1 page) outlining your qualifications and motivation for this project
• Research proposal (max. 3 pages) within the project background described above (own designed proposal)
• CV with contact details of two referees (name, affiliation, position, email address; one referee should be from your current organization)
• Degree certificates* (e.g., Master's and Bachelor's degree) and transcript of records
• Copies of BSc and MSc theses (any language)*, if possible and not confidential

* If you haven’t completed your MSc studies at the time of submission, please substitute the MSc diploma with a written statement by your supervisor specifying the expected completion date and confirming that you are expected to finish on time and send the most recent draft of your thesis.

Please note that applications without these documents will not be considered. More information about our research can be found at the website of Sustainable Food Processing and at the website of Laboratory of Nutrition and Metabolic Epigenetics . Further questions regarding the position should be directed to the project lead Dr. Dr. Fengzheng Gao, fengzheng.gao@hest.ethz.ch with Prof. Dr. Ferdinand von Meyenn ferdinand.vonmeyenn@hest.ethz.ch and Prof. Dr. Alexander Mathys alexander.mathys@hest.ethz.ch in cc.

We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

Posizione dottorale degli studenti – Valutazione di nuove fonti minerali per il trattamento delle carenze micronutrienti negli esseri umani

100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato

Il Laboratorio ETH di Epigenetica, Nutrizione e Metabolismo e Gruppo di Lavorazione Alimentare Sostenibile presso il Dipartimento di Scienze e Tecnologie della Salute gestisce una linea di ricerca strategica congiunta su Microalgae e alimenti a base vegetale in Nutrizione Umana e Salute . Il gruppo Sustainable Food Processing si concentra su un approccio orientato al sistema nella produzione alimentare attraverso la considerazione della catena del valore totale, compresi i bisogni emergenti nella società e il loro impatto ambientale, economico e sociale. Le materie prime innovative sono utilizzate all'interno di concetti di agricoltura urbana e di lavorazione per consentire nuove modalità di approvvigionamento alimentare sostenibile. Il Laboratorio di Epigenetica, Nutrizione e Metabolismo si propone di approfondire il complesso rapporto tra nutrizione, metabolismo e epigeno con tecniche avanzate come le tecniche di sequenziamento monocellulare e di prossima generazione, nonché studi umani e murini in vivo e in vitro e combinare questi con analisi computazionali e bioinformatiche a livello genoma. Con il forte sostegno di questi due gruppi ETH, stiamo reclutando il più presto possibile uno studente di dottorato di talento e altamente motivato sul tema “Novel fonti di minerali per il trattamento delle carenze micronutrienti negli esseri umani”, concentrandosi sull’indagine sull’assorbimento e la biodisponibilità di nuove fonti minerali in vivo in studi clinici.

Sfondo del progetto

La carenza di micronutrienti è un problema di salute globale diffuso, principalmente guidato da un'assunzione dietetica insufficiente. Più di 5 miliardi di persone sono stimate di non consumare abbastanza di almeno un micronutriente. Tra questi, le carenze minerali possono essere particolarmente critiche, vale a dire, le carenze di ferro, calcio, zinco e magnesio, che sono particolarmente comuni nei paesi a basso e medio reddito a causa di diete poco minerali e riguardano principalmente donne e bambini.

I minerali alimentari sono tipicamente ottenuti da una varietà di alimenti tra cui prodotti a base di animali come carne, latticini e frutti di mare, e alimenti a base vegetale come legumi, cereali, noci, semi e verdure a foglia. Tuttavia, l'affidamento sugli alimenti tradizionali basati sugli animali solleva preoccupazioni relative alla sostenibilità ambientale, considerazioni etiche e preferenze alimentari. Anche se gli alimenti a base vegetale sono generalmente più sostenibili, hanno spesso contenuti minerali più bassi, bioaccessibilità, così come la biodisponibilità a causa della presenza di inibitori di assorbimento come i fiati e i polifenoli. Data queste limitazioni, esiste la necessità di esplorare fonti alimentari alternative, più sostenibili e minerali che possano affrontare efficacemente le carenze minerali globali.

Fonti minerali novelli, come le microalghe, potrebbero essere una ricca fonte di minerali essenziali, tra cui ferro, calcio, zinco e magnesio, insieme a proteine, lipidi, vitamine e altri composti bioattivi. Tuttavia, la biodisponibilità di questi minerali deve essere valutata con studi clinici in vivo prima dell'applicazione su larga scala negli esseri umani.

Descrizione del lavoro

Come studente di dottorato, sarai responsabile della ricerca che si occupa di esplorare l'assorbimento e la biodisponibilità di nuove fonti minerali con studi clinici.
• Riassumere le conoscenze esistenti sui minerali da fonti nuove per la nutrizione umana e la salute
• Pasti di intervento di progettazione (compreso test sensoriale) per studi clinici
• Valutare la bioaccessibilità dei minerali in vitro
• Valutare la biodisponibilità minerale in vitro
• Prove cliniche relative alla nutrizione umana arricchite da nuove fonti minerali (chiave)
• Sostenere le attività didattiche e co-supervise studenti MSc e BSc
• Agire all'interfaccia tra scienza e tecnologia quando supervisionare gli studenti e collaborare con i partner dell'accademia e dell'industria
• Sostenere le domande di sovvenzione per il team e sostenere le attività correlate da Singapore-ETH Centre, Bezos Centre for Sustainable Protein a NUS, ETH World Food System Center WFSC e ETH per lo sviluppo ETH4D centro di competenza

Profilo
• Un MSc in Nutrizione e Salute, Prova Clinica, Scienza Alimentare e Tecnologia (con una forte nutrizione o esperienza clinica), o campi rilevanti
• Una forte passione per la nutrizione e la salute, la sostenibilità e le nuove fonti alimentari
• Competenza e interesse a lavorare con opere correlate all'uomo/clinico (il certificato GCP è obbligatorio, tuttavia, può essere ottenuto dopo l'inizio)
• Esperienza e forte interesse per la valutazione della nutrizione utilizzando modelli in vivo
• Capacità di lavorare in un team dinamico, internazionale e interdisciplinare
• Capacità di collaborare con diverse squadre e partner nazionali e internazionali
• Interessi nel lavorare in modo indipendente e supervisionare gli studenti
• Forte capacità di comunicazione verbale e scritta in inglese
• Curiosità scientifica e motivazione per svolgere un lavoro sperimentale scientificamente rigoroso

Offriamo

Potrai lavorare con un team di ricerca leader su Microalgae e Alimenti a base vegetale in Nutrizione umana e Salute con un forte supporto da entrambi i gruppi ETH. Potrai lavorare con attrezzature di ricerca all'avanguardia in un ambiente di lavoro eccellente e aperto. L'ETH Zurigo e il team offrono eccellenti opportunità di formazione per lo sviluppo della carriera e per le reti forti sia in ambito alimentare che alimentare sostenibile. Il progetto otterrà anche supporto da assistenti di ricerca quando necessario.

Le spese di vita saranno sostenute con uno stipendio mensile standard di dottorato fisso secondo le linee guida ETH .

Apprezziamo la diversità e la sostenibilità

In linea con i nostri valori, ETH Zurich incoraggia una cultura inclusiva. Promuoviamo l'uguaglianza di opportunità, la diversità di valore e nutrire un ambiente di lavoro e di apprendimento in cui i diritti e la dignità di tutto il nostro staff e gli studenti sono rispettati. Visita il nostro sito web Equal Opportunities and Diversity per scoprire come garantiamo un ambiente equo e aperto che permetta a tutti di crescere e fiorire. La sostenibilità è un valore fondamentale per noi – stiamo costantemente lavorando verso un futuro neutro dal clima.

Curioso? Anche noi.

Si prega di notare che accettiamo esclusivamente le applicazioni inviate tramite il nostro portale di applicazioni online. La posizione è aperta agli studenti internazionali. Le applicazioni via e-mail o servizi postali non saranno considerate. La chiamata è aperta fino a identificare un candidato adatto. Non esiste una scadenza chiara per le domande. L'ultima data di partenza è prevista per il 01 settembre 2026, prima la migliore.

Non vediamo l'ora di ricevere la tua applicazione online con i seguenti documenti (in inglese, formato PDF):
• Lettera di motivazione (max. 1 pagina) che illustra le tue qualifiche e motivazione per questo progetto
• Proposta di ricerca (max. 3 pagine) nell'ambito del progetto descritto sopra (proposta di progetto)
• CV con dettagli di contatto di due arbitri (nome, affiliazione, posizione, indirizzo e-mail; un arbitro dovrebbe essere dalla vostra organizzazione attuale)
• Certificati di laurea* (ad esempio, master e Bachelor) e trascrizione dei record
• Copie di tesi di laurea e MSc (qualsiasi lingua)*, se possibile e non confidenziale

* Se non avete completato i vostri studi MSc al momento della presentazione, si prega di sostituire il diploma MSc con una dichiarazione scritta dal vostro supervisore specificando la data di completamento prevista e confermando che si prevede di finire in tempo e inviare la bozza più recente della vostra tesi.

Si prega di notare che le domande senza questi documenti non saranno considerate. Maggiori informazioni sulla nostra ricerca si possono trovare sul sito web di Sustainable Food Processing e sul sito web di Laboratory of Nutrition and Metabolic Epigenetics . Ulteriori domande circa la posizione devono essere indirizzate al progetto guida Dr. Fengzheng Gao, fengzheng.gao@hest.ethz.ch con Prof. Dr. Ferdinand von Meyenn ferdinand.vonmeyenn@hest.ethz.ch e Prof. Dr. Alexander Mathys alexander.mathys@hest.ethz.ch in cc.

Vorremmo sottolineare che la pre-selezione è effettuata dai reclutatori responsabili e non dall'intelligenza artificiale.

Informazioni su ETH Zürich

ETH Zurich è una delle università più importanti del mondo specializzata in
scienza e tecnologia. Siamo rinomati per la nostra eccellente educazione,
ricerca fondamentale all'avanguardia e trasferimento diretto di nuove conoscenze
nella società. Oltre 30.000 persone provenienti da più di 120 paesi
università per essere un luogo che promuove il pensiero indipendente e un
ambiente che ispira eccellenza. Situato nel cuore dell'Europa,
ancora forgiando connessioni in tutto il mondo, lavoriamo insieme a
sviluppare soluzioni per le sfide globali di oggi e domani.

descriptionByLocale.de:
Doktorandenposition - Bewertung neuartiger Mineralquellen zur Behandlung von Mikronährstoffmängeln beim Menschen

100%, Zürich, befristet

Die ETH Zürich Laboratory of Epigenetics, Nutrition and Metabolism and Sustainable Food Processing Group im Department of Health Science and Technology betreibt eine gemeinsame strategische Forschungslinie zu Mikroalgen und pflanzlichen Lebensmitteln in Human Nutrition and Health. Die Gruppe Nachhaltige Lebensmittelverarbeitung konzentriert sich auf einen systemorientierten Ansatz in der Lebensmittelproduktion unter Berücksichtigung der gesamten Wertschöpfungskette, einschließlich der sich abzeichnenden Bedürfnisse der Gesellschaft und ihrer ökologischen, wirtschaftlichen und sozialen Auswirkungen. Innovative Rohstoffe werden in urbanen Landwirtschafts- und Verarbeitungskonzepten eingesetzt, um neue Wege der nachhaltigen Lebensmittelversorgung zu ermöglichen. Das Labor für Epigenetik, Ernährung und Metabolismus zielt darauf ab, Einblicke in die komplexe Beziehung zwischen Ernährung, Stoffwechsel und Epigenom mit fortschrittlichen Techniken wie Einzelzell- und Next-Generation-Sequenzierungstechniken sowie Human- und Maus-In-vivo- und In-vitro-Studien zu gewinnen und diese mit genomweiter computergestützter und bioinformatischer Analyse zu kombinieren. Mit starker Unterstützung dieser beiden ETH-Gruppen rekrutieren wir so schnell wie möglich einen talentierten und hochmotivierten Doktoranden zum Thema „Neue Quellen von Mineralien zur Behandlung von Mikronährstoffmängeln beim Menschen, der sich auf die Untersuchung der Absorption und Bioverfügbarkeit neuer Mineralquellen in vivo in klinischen Studien konzentriert.

Projekthintergrund

Mikronährstoffmangel ist ein weit verbreitetes globales Gesundheitsproblem, das hauptsächlich auf eine unzureichende Nahrungsaufnahme zurückzuführen ist. Es wird geschätzt, dass mehr als 5 Milliarden Menschen nicht genug von mindestens einem Mikronährstoff konsumieren. Unter diesen können Mineralstoffmangel besonders kritisch sein, nämlich Eisen-, Kalzium-, Zink- und Magnesiummangel, die in Ländern mit niedrigem und mittlerem Einkommen aufgrund ihrer mineralstoffarmen Ernährung besonders häufig vorkommen und vor allem Frauen und Kinder betreffen.

Diätetische Mineralien werden typischerweise aus einer Vielzahl von Lebensmitteln erhalten, darunter tierische Produkte wie Fleisch, Milchprodukte und Meeresfrüchte sowie pflanzliche Lebensmittel wie Hülsenfrüchte, Getreide, Nüsse, Samen und Blattgemüse. Die Abhängigkeit von herkömmlichen tierischen Lebensmitteln wirft jedoch Bedenken hinsichtlich der ökologischen Nachhaltigkeit, ethischer Überlegungen und Ernährungspräferenzen auf. Obwohl pflanzliche Lebensmittel im Allgemeinen nachhaltiger sind, haben sie aufgrund des Vorhandenseins von Absorptionshemmern wie Phytaten und Polyphenolen oft einen geringeren Mineralstoffgehalt, eine geringere Biozugänglichkeit sowie eine geringere Bioverfügbarkeit. Angesichts dieser Einschränkungen besteht die Notwendigkeit, alternative, nachhaltigere und mineralreichere Nahrungsquellen zu erforschen, die globale Mineralmangel effektiv beheben können.

Neuartige Mineralquellen, wie Mikroalgen, könnten eine reiche Quelle für essentielle Mineralien sein, einschließlich Eisen, Kalzium, Zink und Magnesium, zusammen mit Proteinen, Lipiden, Vitaminen und anderen bioaktiven Verbindungen. Die Bioverfügbarkeit dieser Mineralien muss jedoch mit klinischen In-vivo-Studien vor einer groß angelegten Anwendung am Menschen bewertet werden.

Stellenbeschreibung

Als Doktorand sind Sie für die Forschung verantwortlich, die auf die Erforschung der Absorption und Bioverfügbarkeit neuer Mineralquellen mit klinischen Studien hinarbeitet.
• Zusammenfassen des vorhandenen Wissens über Mineralien aus neuartigen Quellen für die menschliche Ernährung und Gesundheit
• Gestaltung von Interventionsmahlzeiten (einschließlich sensorischer Tests) für klinische Prüfungen
• Bewertung der Biozugänglichkeit von Mineralien in vitro
• Bewertung der Mineralbioverfügbarkeit in vitro
• Durchführung klinischer Versuche im Zusammenhang mit der menschlichen Ernährung, angereichert mit neuartigen mineralischen Quellen (Schlüssel)
• Unterstützen Sie Lehraktivitäten und betreuen Sie MSc- und BSc-Studenten
• Handeln an der Schnittstelle zwischen Wissenschaft und Technologie bei der Betreuung von Studierenden und der Zusammenarbeit mit Partnern aus Wissenschaft und Industrie
• Unterstützung von Zuschussanträgen für das Team und Unterstützung von Aktivitäten im Zusammenhang mit Singapur-ETH Centre, Bezos Centre for Sustainable Protein at NUS, ETH World Food System Center WFSC und ETH for Development ETH4D Kompetenzzentrum

Profil
• Ein MSc in Ernährung und Gesundheit, klinische Studien, Lebensmittelwissenschaft und -technologie (mit starker Ernährungs- oder klinischer Erfahrung) oder relevanten Bereichen
• Eine starke Leidenschaft für Ernährung und Gesundheit, Nachhaltigkeit und neuartige Nahrungsquellen

descriptionByLocale.fr:
Position des étudiants au doctorat – Évaluation de nouvelles sources minérales pour le traitement des carences en micronutriments chez l'homme

100%, Zurich, durée déterminée

Le Laboratoire d'Epigénétique, Nutrition et Métabolisme de Zurich et le Groupe de la transformation durable des aliments du Département des sciences et de la technologie de la santé gèrent une ligne de recherche stratégique conjointe sur les microalgues et les aliments végétaux dans la nutrition humaine et la santé. Le groupe de la transformation durable des aliments se concentre sur une approche systémique de la production alimentaire en tenant compte de la chaîne de valeur totale, y compris les besoins émergents de la société et leurs incidences environnementales, économiques et sociales. Les matières premières innovantes sont utilisées dans l'agriculture urbaine et les concepts de transformation pour permettre de nouveaux modes d'approvisionnement alimentaire durable. Le Laboratoire d'Epigénétique, de Nutrition et de Métabolisme vise à mieux comprendre la relation complexe entre la nutrition, le métabolisme et l'épigénome avec des techniques avancées telles que les techniques de séquençage monocellulaire et de prochaine génération, ainsi que les études in vivo et in vitro humaines et murines, et à les combiner avec des analyses computationnelles et bio-informatiques à l'échelle du génome. Avec le soutien fort de ces deux groupes d'ETH, nous recrutons dès que possible un doctorant talentueux et très motivé sur le thème «Nouvelles sources de minéraux pour le traitement des carences en micronutriments chez l'homme» en se concentrant sur l'étude de l'absorption et de la biodisponibilité de nouvelles sources minérales in vivo dans les essais cliniques.

Contexte du projet

La carence en micronutriments est un problème de santé mondial généralisé, principalement dû à une alimentation inadéquate. On estime que plus de 5 milliards de personnes ne consomment pas assez d'au moins un micronutriment. Parmi celles-ci, les carences minérales peuvent être particulièrement critiques, à savoir les carences en fer, en calcium, en zinc et en magnésium, qui sont particulièrement courantes dans les pays à faible revenu et à revenu intermédiaire en raison de régimes à faible teneur en minéraux et touchent principalement les femmes et les enfants.

Les minéraux alimentaires sont généralement obtenus à partir de divers aliments, notamment des produits à base d'animaux comme la viande, les produits laitiers et les fruits de mer, et des aliments à base de plantes comme les légumineuses, les céréales, les noix, les graines et les légumes à feuilles. Toutefois, la dépendance à l'égard des aliments traditionnels à base d'animaux soulève des préoccupations liées à la durabilité environnementale, aux considérations éthiques et aux préférences alimentaires. Bien que les aliments à base de plantes soient généralement plus durables, ils ont souvent une teneur minérale inférieure, la bioaccessibilité, ainsi que la biodisponibilité en raison de la présence d'inhibiteurs d'absorption tels que les phytates et les polyphénols. Compte tenu de ces limites, il est nécessaire d'explorer d'autres sources alimentaires, plus durables et plus riches en minéraux, susceptibles de remédier efficacement aux carences minérales mondiales.

De nouvelles sources minérales, comme les microalgues, pourraient être une riche source de minéraux essentiels, notamment le fer, le calcium, le zinc et le magnésium, ainsi que des protéines, des lipides, des vitamines et d'autres composés bioactifs. Cependant, la biodisponibilité de ces minéraux doit être évaluée au moyen d'essais cliniques in vivo avant une application à grande échelle chez l' homme.

Description du poste

En tant qu'étudiant au doctorat, vous serez responsable de la recherche visant à explorer l'absorption et la biodisponibilité de nouvelles sources minérales avec des essais cliniques.
• Résumer les connaissances existantes sur les minéraux provenant de sources nouvelles pour la nutrition et la santé humaines
• Concevoir des repas d'intervention (y compris des tests sensoriels) pour les essais cliniques
• Évaluer la bioaccessibilité des minéraux in vitro
• Évaluer la biodisponibilité minérale in vitro
• Effectuer des essais cliniques liés à la nutrition humaine enrichie en nouvelles sources minérales (clé)
• Soutenir les activités d'enseignement et co-superviser les étudiants en maîtrise et en baccalauréat
• Agir à l'interface entre la science et la technologie en supervisant les étudiants et en collaborant avec des partenaires du milieu universitaire et de l'industrie
• Demandes de subvention d'appui à l'équipe et activités connexes du Centre Singapour-ETH, du Centre Bezos pour les protéines durables au NUS, du Centre du système alimentaire mondial de l'ETH et du Centre de compétences ETH4D

Profil
• Une maîtrise en nutrition et santé, essais cliniques, science et technologie alimentaires (avec une solide expérience nutritionnelle ou clinique) ou des domaines pertinents
• Une forte passion pour la nutrition et la santé, la durabilité et de nouvelles sources alimentaires
• Expertise et intérêt pour les travaux humains/cliniques (le certificat GCP est obligatoire, cependant, peut être obtenu après le début)
• Expérience et grand intérêt pour l'évaluation nutritionnelle à l'aide de modèles in vivo
• Capacité de travailler dans une équipe dynamique, internationale et interdisciplinaire
• Capacité de collaborer avec différentes équipes et partenaires nationaux et internationaux
• Intérêt à travailler indépendamment et à superviser les étudiants
• Fortes compétences en communication verbale et écrite en anglais
• Curiosité scientifique et motivation à effectuer un travail expérimental scientifiquement rigoureux

Nous offrons

Vous travaillerez avec une équipe de recherche de premier plan sur les microalgues et les aliments végétaux dans la nutrition et la santé humaines, avec le soutien fort des deux groupes ETH. Vous travaillerez avec des équipements de recherche de pointe dans un excellent environnement de travail ouvert. Eth Zurich et l'équipe offrent d'excellentes possibilités de formation pour le développement de carrière et de solides réseaux dans l'alimentation et la nutrition durables. Le projet recevra également l'appui d'assistants de recherche au besoin.

Les frais de subsistance seront supportés avec un salaire mensuel standard de doctorat selon les lignes directrices de l'ETH .

Nous apprécions la diversité et la durabilité

La durabilité est une valeur fondamentale pour nous – nous travaillons constamment vers un avenir neutre sur le plan climatique.

D'autres questions concernant le poste doivent être adressées au directeur du projet, Dr. Fengzheng Gao, fengzheng.gao@hest.ethz.ch, avec le professeur Dr. Ferdinand von Meyenn ferdinand.vonmeyenn@hest.ethz.ch et le professeur Dr. Alexander Mathys alexander.mathys@hest.ethz.ch in cc.

Nous tenons à souligner que la présélection est effectuée par les recruteurs responsables et non par l'intelligence artificielle.

mais forgeant des liens partout dans le monde, nous travaillons ensemble pour

jobs.description:
PhD opening in material science of stone conservation

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

The Chair for Physical Chemistry of Building Materials has one opening for PhD. position on the topic of stone conservation, in particular the mechanisms of contour scaling. This PhD is part of the collaborative project “Spatially graded 3D printing to elucidate contour scaling of building stones”. It aims at elucidating the mechanism of contour scaling on building stone, establishing on-site monitoring methods and testing possible treatments for it. The selected student will collaborate with another PhD candidate funded in the scheme and employed at the Chair for Digital Building Technologies in the Department of Architecture.

Project background

This project aims to establish and validate a novel experimental approach to the study of stone deterioration by leveraging powder-bed 3D printing of stone-like materials. This enables the creation of spatially graded samples mimicking natural stones and their alteration through weathering. Most importantly, this can be done in a repetitive way and with systematic variations of the defect, flaws and inhomogeneities known to play an essential role in stone deterioration.

The specific stone deterioration mechanism that will be investigated is contour scaling, a process of particular concern to molasse sandstones largely used in the Swiss plateau. It leads to loss of cohesion below the exposed surface, at a depth in the range of some millimetres to several centimetres. It leads to highly inhomogeneous properties that our 3D printing approach would be able to mimic for the first time.

The 3D printing will begin using an innovative and large-scale 3D powder bed printer developed by the Chair for Digital Building Technologies, and will be advanced for the purpose of this project by the other PhD student.

Job description
• The present PhD student will use such 3D printed stones in the unique testing facilities of the Chair for Physical Chemistry of Building Materials
• This will enable the reproduction under laboratory conditions of harsh events that condition the weathering of building stones on monuments
• That study will be complemented by method development to enable rapid detection of contour scales on site, in addition to exploring possible means of halting the propagation and/or formation of such contour scales

Profile
• The successful candidate should have a keen interest, or preferably experience in heritage conservation science
• They should additionally hold a Masters degree in conservation science, material science, chemistry, chemical engineering, civil engineering, or conservation architecture
• In any case good experimental skills are a must
• An excellent oral and written level of English is essential
• Conversational knowledge of German is an advantage, but desire to learn it is a must
• As the project involves collaboration between groups in addition to field practitioners, very good communication skills and willingness to collaborate with other researchers is essential

Our highly diverse and international group also offers many networking opportunities through academic societies such as RILEM, industry connections, as well as internal ETH connections. We would also like to get to know you better and would therefore ask you to send us a short video of no more than two minutes. We do not expect a professionally produced video; even a recording made on a smartphone is perfectly sufficient. A short introduction of yourself and why you are interested in the position should be included. Please then upload the video to a platform of your choice (Dropbox, YouTube, Vimeo, Google Drive, etc.) and include the relevant URL link in your cover letter.

Apertura del dottorato in scienze materiali di conservazione della pietra

100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato

La sedia per Chimica Fisica dei Materiali Edili ha un'apertura per la posizione di dottorato sul tema della conservazione della pietra, in particolare i meccanismi di contorno scaling. Questo PhD fa parte del progetto collaborativo “Spatially graded 3D Print to elucidate cotour scaling of building stone”. Esso mira a elucidare il meccanismo di contorno scaling su pietra da costruzione, stabilendo metodi di monitoraggio in loco e testando possibili trattamenti per esso. Lo studente selezionato collaborerà con un altro candidato di dottorato finanziato nello schema e impiegato presso il Chair for Digital Building Technologies nel Dipartimento di Architettura.

Sfondo del progetto

Questo progetto mira a stabilire e convalidare un nuovo approccio sperimentale allo studio del deterioramento della pietra sfruttando la stampa 3D in polvere di materiali simili a pietre. Ciò consente la creazione di campioni di livello spaziale che imitano le pietre naturali e la loro alterazione attraverso le intemperie. Soprattutto, questo può essere fatto in modo ripetitivo e con variazioni sistematiche del difetto, dei difetti e delle omogeneità note per svolgere un ruolo essenziale nel deterioramento della pietra.

Il meccanismo specifico di deterioramento della pietra che verrà indagato è la scagliatura del contorno, un processo di particolare preoccupazione per la molasse arenaria largamente utilizzata nell'altopiano svizzero. Essa porta alla perdita di coesione sotto la superficie esposta, a una profondità nella gamma di alcuni millimetri a diversi centimetri. Porta a proprietà altamente inomogenee che il nostro approccio di stampa 3D sarebbe in grado di imitare per la prima volta.

La stampa 3D inizierà ad utilizzare una stampante 3D innovativa e su larga scala sviluppata dalla Chair for Digital Building Technologies, e sarà avanzata allo scopo di questo progetto dall'altro dottorando.

Descrizione del lavoro
• L'attuale studente di dottorato utilizzerà tali pietre stampate 3D negli impianti di prova unici della sedia per chimica fisica dei materiali da costruzione
• Ciò consentirà la riproduzione in condizioni di laboratorio di eventi difficili che condizionano il tempo di costruire pietre su monumenti
• Tale studio sarà completato dallo sviluppo dei metodi per consentire un rapido rilevamento delle scale di contorno in loco, oltre ad esplorare possibili mezzi di fermare la propagazione e/o la formazione di tali scale di contorno

Profilo
• Il candidato di successo dovrebbe avere un interesse acuto, o preferibilmente esperienza nella scienza della conservazione del patrimonio
• Essi dovrebbero inoltre tenere un master in scienze della conservazione, scienza materiale, chimica, ingegneria chimica, ingegneria civile, o architettura di conservazione
• In ogni caso le buone capacità sperimentali sono un must
• Un eccellente livello orale e scritto di inglese è essenziale
• La conoscenza conversazionale del tedesco è un vantaggio, ma il desiderio di imparare è un must
• Poiché il progetto coinvolge la collaborazione tra gruppi oltre ai professionisti del campo, le capacità di comunicazione molto buone e la volontà di collaborare con altri ricercatori è essenziale

Offriamo

La Cattedra di Chimica Fisica dei Materiali Edili all'interno dell'Istituto per i Materiali Edili offre molte possibilità per avviare una carriera di ricerca accademica o industriale nella tecnologia del cemento e del cemento, con una forte base nella chimica dei materiali e nella reologia. Il nostro gruppo altamente diversificato e internazionale offre anche molte opportunità di networking attraverso società accademiche come RILEM, connessioni del settore, così come connessioni ETH interne. Siamo impegnati nella diversità consentendo flessibilità nelle ore di lavoro, negli uffici domestici e in altre misure per garantire che i membri del team possano svolgere adeguatamente i loro ruoli.

Apprezziamo la diversità e la sostenibilità

In linea con i nostri valori, ETH Zurich incoraggia una cultura inclusiva. Promuoviamo l'uguaglianza di opportunità, la diversità di valore e nutrire un ambiente di lavoro e di apprendimento in cui i diritti e la dignità di tutto il nostro staff e gli studenti sono rispettati. Visita il nostro sito web Equal Opportunities and Diversity per scoprire come garantiamo un ambiente equo e aperto che permetta a tutti di crescere e fiorire. La sostenibilità è un valore fondamentale per noi – stiamo costantemente lavorando verso un futuro neutro dal clima.

Curioso? Anche noi.

Non vediamo l'ora di ricevere la tua domanda online con i seguenti documenti:
• Lettera di copertura
• CV
• Nomi e informazioni di contatto (indirizzo e-mail) di tre riferimenti

Vorremmo anche conoscervi meglio e vi chiederemmo di inviarci un breve video di non più di due minuti. Non ci aspettiamo un video prodotto professionalmente; anche una registrazione fatta su uno smartphone è perfettamente sufficiente. Una breve introduzione di te stesso e perché sei interessato alla posizione dovrebbe essere incluso. Si prega di caricare il video su una piattaforma di vostra scelta (Dropbox, YouTube, Vimeo, Google Drive, ecc.) e includere il relativo link URL nella vostra lettera di copertura.

Ulteriori informazioni sulla Chimica Fisica dei Materiali Edili si possono trovare sul nostro sito . Le domande relative alla posizione devono essere indirizzate al Dr. Timothy Wangler, Tel +41 44 633 2943 o e-mail twangler@ethz.ch (nessuna domanda).

Si prega di notare che accettiamo esclusivamente le applicazioni inviate tramite il nostro portale di applicazioni online. Le applicazioni via e-mail o servizi postali non saranno considerate.

Informazioni su ETH Zürich

ETH Zurich è una delle università più importanti del mondo specializzata in
scienza e tecnologia. Siamo rinomati per la nostra eccellente educazione,
ricerca fondamentale all'avanguardia e trasferimento diretto di nuove conoscenze
nella società. Oltre 30.000 persone provenienti da più di 120 paesi
università per essere un luogo che promuove il pensiero indipendente e un
ambiente che ispira eccellenza. Situato nel cuore dell'Europa,
ancora forgiando connessioni in tutto il mondo, lavoriamo insieme a
sviluppare soluzioni per le sfide globali di oggi e domani.

The 3D printing will begin using an innovative and large-scale 3D powder bed printer developed by the Chair for Digital Building Technologies, and will be advanced for the purpose of this project by the other PhD student.

Job description
• The present PhD student will use such 3D printed stones in the unique testing facilities of the Chair for Physical Chemistry of Building Materials
• This will enable the reproduction under laboratory conditions of harsh events that condition the weathering of building stones on monuments
• That study will be complemented by method development to enable rapid detection of contour scales on site, in addition to exploring possible means of halting the propagation and/or formation of such contour scales

Profile
• The successful candidate should have a keen interest, or preferably experience in heritage conservation science
• They should additionally hold a Masters degree in conservation science, material science, chemistry, chemical engineering, civil engineering, or conservation architecture
• In any case good experimental skills are a must
• An excellent oral and written level of English is essential
• Conversational knowledge of German is an advantage, but desire to learn it is a must
• As the project involves collaboration between groups in addition to field practitioners, very good communication skills and willingness to collaborate with other researchers is essential

The Chair of Physical Chemistry of Building Materials within the Institute for Building Materials offers many chances for jump-starting an academic or industrial research career in cement and concrete technology, with a strong basis in materials chemistry and rheology. Our highly diverse and international group also offers many networking opportunities through academic societies such as RILEM, industry connections, as well as internal ETH connections. PhD Eröffnung in Materialwissenschaft der Steinkonservierung

100%, Zürich, befristet

Der Lehrstuhl für Physikalische Chemie von Baustoffen hat eine Position zum Thema Steinschutz, insbesondere zu den Mechanismen der Konturskalierung. Diese Promotion ist Teil des Verbundprojekts „Räumlich abgestufter 3D-Druck zur Aufklärung der Konturskalierung von Bausteinen. Es zielt darauf ab, den Mechanismus der Konturskalierung auf dem Baustein aufzuklären, Überwachungsmethoden vor Ort zu etablieren und mögliche Behandlungen dafür zu testen. Der ausgewählte Student wird mit einem anderen Doktoranden zusammenarbeiten, der im Rahmen des Programms finanziert und am Lehrstuhl für digitale Gebäudetechnologien in der Abteilung für Architektur beschäftigt ist.

Projekthintergrund

Dieses Projekt zielt darauf ab, einen neuartigen experimentellen Ansatz zur Untersuchung der Steinverschlechterung durch den Einsatz des Pulverbett-3D-Drucks von steinähnlichen Materialien zu etablieren und zu validieren. Dies ermöglicht die Schaffung von räumlich abgestuften Proben, die Natursteine nachahmen und deren Veränderung durch Verwitterung. Am wichtigsten ist, dass dies auf wiederholte Weise und mit systematischen Variationen des Defekts, der Fehler und Inhomogenitäten erfolgen kann, von denen bekannt ist, dass sie eine wesentliche Rolle bei der Steinverschlechterung spielen.

Der spezifische Steinverschlechterungsmechanismus, der untersucht wird, ist die Konturskalierung, ein Prozess, der für Melassesandsteine, die hauptsächlich auf dem Schweizer Plateau verwendet werden, von besonderer Bedeutung ist. Es führt zu einem Verlust des Zusammenhalts unterhalb der exponierten Oberfläche in einer Tiefe im Bereich von einigen Millimetern bis zu mehreren Zentimetern. Es führt zu sehr inhomogenen Eigenschaften, die unser 3D-Druck-Ansatz zum ersten Mal nachahmen könnte.

Der 3D-Druck wird mit einem innovativen und großformatigen 3D-Pulverbettdrucker beginnen, der vom Lehrstuhl für digitale Gebäudetechnologien entwickelt wurde, und wird für den Zweck dieses Projekts von dem anderen Doktoranden weiterentwickelt.

Stellenbeschreibung
• Der jetzige Doktorand wird solche 3D-gedruckten Steine in den einzigartigen Testeinrichtungen des Lehrstuhls für Physikalische Chemie von Baustoffen verwenden.
• Dies ermöglicht die Reproduktion von harten Ereignissen unter Laborbedingungen, die die Verwitterung von Bausteinen auf Denkmälern beeinflussen.
• Diese Studie wird durch die Entwicklung von Methoden ergänzt, die eine schnelle Erkennung von Konturskalen vor Ort ermöglichen, zusätzlich zur Untersuchung möglicher Mittel zur Verhinderung der Ausbreitung und/oder Bildung solcher Konturskalen.

Profil

• Sie sollten zusätzlich einen Master-Abschluss in Naturschutzwissenschaften, Materialwissenschaften, Chemie, Chemieingenieurwesen, Bauingenieurwesen oder Naturschutzarchitektur haben
• Gute experimentelle Fähigkeiten sind in jedem Fall ein Muss
• Ein ausgezeichnetes mündliches und schriftliches Englischniveau ist unerlässlich
• Deutschkenntnisse im Gespräch sind von Vorteil, aber der Wunsch, es zu lernen, ist ein Muss
• Da das Projekt die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Gruppen und Praktikern umfasst, sind sehr gute Kommunikationsfähigkeiten und die Bereitschaft zur Zusammenarbeit mit anderen Forschern unerlässlich.

Ouverture du doctorat en science matérielle de la conservation de la pierre

100%, Zurich, durée déterminée

La chaire de chimie physique des matériaux de construction a une ouverture pour le doctorat. position sur le thème de la conservation de la pierre, en particulier les mécanismes de l'échelle de contour. Ce doctorat s'inscrit dans le cadre du projet de collaboration. Il vise à élucider le mécanisme d'échelle des contours sur la pierre de construction, à établir des méthodes de surveillance sur place et à tester les traitements possibles pour elle. L'étudiant sélectionné collaborera avec un autre candidat au doctorat financé dans le cadre du programme et sera employé à la Chaire de technologies de construction numérique du Département d'architecture.

Contexte du projet

Ce projet vise à établir et à valider une nouvelle approche expérimentale de l'étude de la détérioration de la pierre en tirant parti de l'impression 3D par lit de poudre de matériaux de type pierre. Cela permet la création d'échantillons classés dans l'espace mimichant les pierres naturelles et leur altération par l'altération. Plus important encore, cela peut être fait de manière répétitive et avec des variations systématiques des défauts, défauts et inhomogénéités connus pour jouer un rôle essentiel dans la détérioration de la pierre.

Le mécanisme spécifique de détérioration de la pierre qui sera étudié est l'échelle de contour, un processus particulièrement préoccupant pour les grès molasques largement utilisés sur le plateau suisse. Elle entraîne une perte de cohésion sous la surface exposée, à une profondeur de quelques millimètres à plusieurs centimètres. Il conduit à des propriétés hautement inhomogènes que notre approche d'impression 3D pourrait imiter pour la première fois.

L'impression 3D commencera à utiliser une imprimante 3D innovante et à grande échelle développée par la Chaire des technologies de construction numérique, et sera avancée aux fins de ce projet par l'autre doctorant.

Description du poste
• Le doctorant actuel utilisera ces pierres imprimées 3D dans les installations d'essai uniques de la Chaire de chimie physique des matériaux de construction
• Cela permettra la reproduction dans des conditions de laboratoire d'événements difficiles qui conditionnent l'altération des pierres de construction sur les monuments
• Cette étude sera complétée par l'élaboration de méthodes permettant la détection rapide des échelles de contour sur place, en plus d'explorer les moyens possibles d'arrêter la propagation et/ou la formation de ces échelles de contour

Profil
• Le candidat retenu devrait avoir un vif intérêt ou une expérience de préférence en sciences de la conservation du patrimoine
• Ils devraient également détenir une maîtrise en sciences de la conservation, sciences des matériaux, chimie, génie chimique, génie civil ou architecture de conservation
• En tout état de cause, de bonnes compétences expérimentales sont indispensables.
• Un excellent niveau d'anglais oral et écrit est essentiel
• La connaissance conversationnelle de l'allemand est un avantage, mais le désir d'apprendre est un must
• Comme le projet implique la collaboration entre les groupes en plus des praticiens de terrain, de très bonnes compétences en communication et la volonté de collaborer avec d'autres chercheurs sont essentielles

Nous offrons

La chaire de chimie physique des matériaux de construction de l'Institut des matériaux de construction offre de nombreuses chances de démarrer une carrière universitaire ou industrielle de recherche en ciment et en technologie du béton, avec une base solide en chimie des matériaux et en rhéologie. jobs.description:
PhD position in Modeling and Control of Nonlinear Dynamical Systems from Data

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

The Chair in Nonlinear Dynamics at ETH Zürich is inviting applications for a 100% PhD position in the development and application of nonlinear dynamical systems methods for complex physical problems known only from data. The objective is to provide efficient, theoretically sound, fast, and directly interpretable alternative in modelling to the black-box approach of neural networks.

Job description
• The selected candidate will work on the furhter development of spectral submanifold (SSM) methods, aiming to further develop concepts in nonlinear model reduction
• Possible research directions include the development of nonlinear modelling and control approaches for fluid-structure interactions, material with memory, soft robotics, tele-operated systems, lightweight space structures, and turbulent flows
• Ongoing and prior work in related areas by the Chair in Nonlinear Dynamics can be found at the group website
• The position will be based at either the Department of Mechanical and Process Engineering or the Department of Mathematics, depending on the candidate’s background and preferences
• The starting date is flexible but an early start is preferred

Profile
• The successful candidate is expected to have a master's degree in mechanical engineering, applied mathematics, physics, or related areas
• Strong mathematical skills (evidenced by high grades) are required and will be tested in technical interviews.
• Prior research experience in problems related to fluid mechanics, structural vibrations, model reduction or control is expected
• Experience in nonlinear dynamical systems methods and data-driven analysis is a plus

We offer
• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Researcher – Tactile Sensing for Dexterous Manipulation

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

The Soft Robotics Lab within the Institute of Robotics and Intelligent Systems at ETH Zurich is inviting applications for a postdoctoral position within an industry-funded research collaboration. We are looking for an accomplished, hands-on researcher to lead the development of compact, durable tactile sensors for dexterous robotic hands, so that these hands can manipulate reliably even where vision falls short in unstructured, real-world settings. Our lab's goal is to build, model, and control robots in a fundamentally different way, so that they become more flexible, dexterous, capable, and adapt better to their environment. The lab has showcased its research in robotic design and algorithms through real-world applications such as a robotic fish for underwater locomotion and soft robotic hands for versatile object and scene manipulation .

Project background

Cameras alone are not enough for reliable manipulation: clutter, occlusion, and deformable objects routinely defeat vision-based approaches in real-world settings. The sense of touch closes this gap, yet today's tactile sensors still fall short of the compactness, durability, and measurement quality that dexterous robotic hands demand. As the postdoctoral researcher on this project, you will put tactile sensing at the center of the hand's design rather than treating it as an afterthought. Building on the lab's experience integrating proprioceptive and tactile sensing into tendon-driven, musculoskeletal robotic hands, you will design, fabricate, and characterize sensor modules that provide multi-axis force information, and drive their integration into a working hand platform.

Job description
• You will lead the design, fabrication, and characterization of compact tactile sensing modules that provide multi-axis force information, fit within a human hand form factor, and remain robust under the wear of real-world manipulation
• You will survey and benchmark different tactile sensing modalities against each other, selecting the approaches best suited to the project's requirements
• You will integrate the resulting sensors into one of the lab's existing tendon-driven robotic hand platforms, optimizing readout electronics and packaging for seamless system integration
• You will design representative bench- and task-level benchmarks and demonstrate closed-loop tactile behaviors for real-time manipulation control
• As the senior researcher on the project, you will co-supervise the PhD student and master's students working alongside you, take ownership of driving the work end to end, and lead dissemination through publication in top robotics venues

Profile

You are an accomplished, hands-on researcher who wants to make a real difference with your work You are highly independent and assertive in defending your research direction, while thriving when collaborating with and supporting others. Through your prior experience, you have ideally already demonstrated:
• A completed PhD in robotics, mechanical engineering, mechatronics, electrical engineering, or a closely related field
• A strong, published track record of hands-on hardware research: designing, fabricating, and experimentally validating physical sensing or actuation systems in the real world
• Demonstrated expertise in at least one relevant sensing modality (e.g. tactile, force, or optical sensing), and comfort working across electronics, mechanical design, fabrication, and signal processing
• A track record of peer-reviewed publications in leading robotics venues that demonstrate both technical depth and real-world validation of results
• Prior experience mentoring or co-supervising PhD or master's students, and a collaborative, supportive mindset
• Strong written and spoken English, and comfort communicating results to an industry partner as well as an academic audience
• Background or experience in tactile sensing or dexterous manipulation is a plus

We offer

• The opportunity to lead a component of an active industry research collaboration, with direct exposure to real-world deployment requirements alongside publication-quality academic research

100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato

Il Soft Robotics Lab all'interno dell'Istituto di Robotica e Sistemi Intelligenti dell'ETH di Zurigo invita le applicazioni per una posizione post-dottorale all'interno di una collaborazione di ricerca finanziata dal settore. Siamo alla ricerca di un ricercatore esperto e pratico per condurre lo sviluppo di sensori tattili compatti e durevoli per mani robotiche destrezza, in modo che queste mani possano manipolare in modo affidabile anche quando la visione cade in ambienti non strutturati e reali. L'obiettivo del nostro laboratorio è quello di costruire, modellare e controllare i robot in modo fondamentalmente diverso, in modo che diventino più flessibili, dexterous, capaci, e si adattano meglio al loro ambiente. Il laboratorio ha presentato la sua ricerca nel design robotico e algoritmi attraverso applicazioni reali come un pesce robotico per locomozione subacquea e mani robotiche morbide per la manipolazione versatile di oggetti e scene.

Sfondo del progetto

Le telecamere da sole non sono sufficienti per una manipolazione affidabile: ingombri, occlusioni e oggetti deformabili di routine sconfiggere approcci basati sulla visione nelle impostazioni del mondo reale. Il senso del tatto chiude questo divario, ma i sensori tattili di oggi cadono ancora a corto della compattezza, della durata e della qualità di misura che le mani robotiche destrezza richiedono. Come ricercatore postdoctoral su questo progetto, si metterà tattile sensibilità al centro del disegno della mano piuttosto che trattarlo come un ripensamento. Basandosi sull'esperienza del laboratorio che integra il rilevamento propriocettivo e tattile in mani robotiche muscolo-scheletriche, disegnate, fabbricate e caratterizzate i moduli dei sensori che forniscono informazioni sulla forza multiassiale e spingono la loro integrazione in una piattaforma di lavoro.

Descrizione del lavoro
• Condurrai la progettazione, la fabbricazione e la caratterizzazione di moduli tattili compatti che forniscono informazioni di forza multiasse, si adattano all'interno di un fattore di forma della mano umana e rimangono robusti sotto l'usura della manipolazione del mondo reale
• Indagherai e benchmark diverse modalità di rilevamento tattile l'una contro l'altra, selezionando gli approcci più adatti ai requisiti del progetto
• Integrerai i sensori che ne derivano in una delle piattaforme di mani robotiche a tendina esistenti, ottimizzando l'elettronica di lettura e l'imballaggio per l'integrazione del sistema senza soluzione di continuità
• Progetterai benchmark rappresentativi a livello di banco e di lavoro e dimostrerai comportamenti tattili a ciclo chiuso per il controllo della manipolazione in tempo reale
• Come ricercatore senior sul progetto, co-superviserai gli studenti del dottorato e gli studenti del master che lavorano accanto a te, prendere la proprietà di guidare la fine del lavoro alla fine, e condurre la diffusione attraverso la pubblicazione in luoghi di robotica superiore

• Un dottorato completo in robotica, ingegneria meccanica, meccatronica, ingegneria elettrica, o un campo strettamente correlato
• Un forte e pubblicato track record di hands-on di ricerca hardware: progettazione, fabbricazione e validazione sperimentale di sistemi di rilevamento fisico o di attuazione nel mondo reale
• Competenza dimostrata in almeno una modalità di rilevamento rilevante (ad esempio tattile, forza o sensibilità ottica) e comfort di lavoro in elettronica, progettazione meccanica, fabbricazione e elaborazione dei segnali

Postdoctoral Researcher – Tactile Sensing for Dexterous Manipulation

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

The Soft Robotics Lab within the Institute of Robotics and Intelligent Systems at ETH Zurich is inviting applications for a postdoctoral position within an industry-funded research collaboration. We are looking for an accomplished, hands-on researcher to lead the development of compact, durable tactile sensors for dexterous robotic hands, so that these hands can manipulate reliably even where vision falls short in unstructured, real-world settings. Our lab's goal is to build, model, and control robots in a fundamentally different way, so that they become more flexible, dexterous, capable, and adapt better to their environment. The lab has showcased its research in robotic design and algorithms through real-world applications such as a robotic fish for underwater locomotion and soft robotic hands for versatile object and scene manipulation .

Project background

Cameras alone are not enough for reliable manipulation: clutter, occlusion, and deformable objects routinely defeat vision-based approaches in real-world settings. The sense of touch closes this gap, yet today's tactile sensors still fall short of the compactness, durability, and measurement quality that dexterous robotic hands demand. As the postdoctoral researcher on this project, you will put tactile sensing at the center of the hand's design rather than treating it as an afterthought. Building on the lab's experience integrating proprioceptive and tactile sensing into tendon-driven, musculoskeletal robotic hands, you will design, fabricate, and characterize sensor modules that provide multi-axis force information, and drive their integration into a working hand platform.

Job description
• You will lead the design, fabrication, and characterization of compact tactile sensing modules that provide multi-axis force information, fit within a human hand form factor, and remain robust under the wear of real-world manipulation
• You will survey and benchmark different tactile sensing modalities against each other, selecting the approaches best suited to the project's requirements
• You will integrate the resulting sensors into one of the lab's existing tendon-driven robotic hand platforms, optimizing readout electronics and packaging for seamless system integration
• You will design representative bench- and task-level benchmarks and demonstrate closed-loop tactile behaviors for real-time manipulation control
• As the senior researcher on the project, you will co-supervise the PhD student and master's students working alongside you, take ownership of driving the work end to end, and lead dissemination through publication in top robotics venues

Profile

You are an accomplished, hands-on researcher who wants to make a real difference with your work You are highly independent and assertive in defending your research direction, while thriving when collaborating with and supporting others. Through your prior experience, you have ideally already demonstrated:
• A completed PhD in robotics, mechanical engineering, mechatronics, electrical engineering, or a closely related field
• A strong, published track record of hands-on hardware research: designing, fabricating, and experimentally validating physical sensing or actuation systems in the real world
• Demonstrated expertise in at least one relevant sensing modality (e.g. tactile, force, or optical sensing), and comfort working across electronics, mechanical design, fabrication, and signal processing
• A track record of peer-reviewed publications in leading robotics venues that demonstrate both technical depth and real-world validation of results
• Prior experience mentoring or co-supervising PhD or master's students, and a collaborative, supportive mindset
• Strong written and spoken English, and comfort communicating results to an industry partner as well as an academic audience
• Background or experience in tactile sensing or dexterous manipulation is a plus

• The opportunity to lead a component of an active industry research collaboration, with direct exposure to real-world deployment requirements alongside publication-quality academic research

Postdoktorandin – Taktile Sensing für geschickte Manipulation

100%, Zürich, befristet

Das Soft Robotics Lab des Instituts für Robotik und Intelligente Systeme der ETH Zürich lädt zu Bewerbungen für eine Postdoc-Stelle im Rahmen einer industriefinanzierten Forschungskooperation ein. Wir suchen einen erfahrenen, praktischen Forscher, der die Entwicklung kompakter, langlebiger taktiler Sensoren für geschickte Roboterhände leitet, so dass diese Hände zuverlässig manipulieren können, auch wenn das Sehen in unstrukturierten, realen Umgebungen zu kurz kommt. Ziel unseres Labors ist es, Roboter grundlegend anders zu bauen, zu modellieren und zu steuern, so dass sie flexibler, geschickter, fähiger werden und sich besser an ihre Umgebung anpassen. Das Labor hat seine Forschung im Bereich Roboterdesign und Algorithmen durch reale Anwendungen wie einen Roboterfisch für die Unterwasserbewegung und weiche Roboterhände für eine vielseitige Objekt- und Szenenmanipulation gezeigt.

Projekthintergrund

Kameras allein sind nicht genug für eine zuverlässige Manipulation: Unordnung, Okklusion und verformbare Objekte besiegen routinemäßig visionäre Ansätze in realen Umgebungen. Der Tastsinn schließt diese Lücke, doch die heutigen taktilen Sensoren verfehlen immer noch die Kompaktheit, Langlebigkeit und Messqualität, die geschickte Roboterhände verlangen. Als Postdoktorand in diesem Projekt werden Sie die taktile Wahrnehmung in den Mittelpunkt des Handdesigns stellen, anstatt sie als nachträglichen Einfall zu behandeln. Aufbauend auf der Erfahrung des Labors, propriozeptive und taktile Sensorik in sehnengesteuerte, muskuloskelettale Roboterhände zu integrieren, entwerfen, fertigen und charakterisieren Sie Sensormodule, die mehrachsige Kraftinformationen liefern und ihre Integration in eine Arbeitshandplattform vorantreiben.

Stellenbeschreibung
• Sie werden das Design, die Herstellung und die Charakterisierung von kompakten taktilen Sensormodulen leiten, die mehrachsige Kraftinformationen liefern, in einen menschlichen Handformfaktor passen und unter dem Verschleiß der realen Manipulation robust bleiben.
• Sie werden verschiedene taktile Sensing-Modalitäten gegeneinander untersuchen und vergleichen und die für die Anforderungen des Projekts am besten geeigneten Ansätze auswählen
• Sie integrieren die resultierenden Sensoren in eine der bestehenden sehnengesteuerten Roboterhandplattformen des Labors und optimieren die Ausleseelektronik und -verpackung für eine nahtlose Systemintegration
• Sie entwerfen repräsentative Bench- und Task-Level-Benchmarks und demonstrieren ein geschlossenes taktiles Verhalten für die Echtzeit-Manipulationskontrolle
• Als leitender Forscher des Projekts betreuen Sie den Doktoranden und die Masterstudenten, die neben Ihnen arbeiten, übernehmen die Verantwortung, die Arbeit von Ende zu Ende voranzutreiben, und leiten die Verbreitung durch Veröffentlichung in Top-Robotik-Veranstaltungen.

Profil

Sie sind ein versierter, praktischer Forscher, der mit Ihrer Arbeit einen echten Unterschied machen möchte Sie sind sehr unabhängig und selbstbewusst bei der Verteidigung Ihrer Forschungsrichtung, während Sie bei der Zusammenarbeit und Unterstützung anderer erfolgreich sind. Durch Ihre Vorerfahrung haben Sie idealerweise bereits gezeigt:
• Ein abgeschlossener PhD in Robotik, Maschinenbau, Mechatronik, Elektrotechnik oder einem eng verwandten Bereich
• Eine starke, veröffentlichte Erfolgsbilanz der praktischen Hardwareforschung: Entwurf, Herstellung und experimentelle Validierung von physikalischen Sensor- oder Betätigungssystemen in der realen Welt
• Nachgewiesene Expertise in mindestens einer relevanten Sensormodalität (z. B. taktile, Kraft- oder optische Sensorik) und Komfortarbeit in Elektronik, mechanischem Design, Fertigung und Signalverarbeitung
• Eine Erfolgsbilanz von Peer-Review-Publikationen in führenden Robotik-Locations, die sowohl die technische Tiefe als auch die Validierung der Ergebnisse in der Praxis belegen
• Vorherige Erfahrung Mentoring oder Co-Betreuung PhD oder Master-Studenten, und eine kollaborative, unterstützende Denkweise
• Starkes geschriebenes und gesprochenes Englisch und die Kommunikation der Ergebnisse mit einem Industriepartner sowie einem akademischen Publikum
• Hintergrund oder Erfahrung in der taktilen Wahrnehmung oder geschickte Manipulation ist ein Plus

Wir bieten

• Die Möglichkeit, eine Komponente einer aktiven Industrieforschungskooperation zu leiten, mit direktem Kontakt zu realen Bereitstellungsanforderungen neben der akademischen Forschung in Publikationsqualität
• Sie können zahlreiche Vorteile erwarten, wie Saisontickets für den öffentlichen Nahverkehr und Carsharing, eine breite Palette von Sportangeboten des ASVZ, Kinderbetreuung und attraktive Pensionsleistungen.
• Sie arbeiten in einem multidisziplinären Team und haben Zugang zu einem erstklassigen Labor, modernsten Fertigungsanlagen und dem breiteren Robotik-Ökosystem der ETH Zürich

Wir legen Wert auf Vielfalt und Nachhaltigkeit

Besuchen Sie unsere Website für Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt, um herauszufinden, wie wir ein faires und offenes Umfeld gewährleisten, in dem jeder wachsen und gedeihen kann. Nachhaltigkeit ist für uns ein zentraler Wert – wir arbeiten konsequent auf eine klimaneutrale Zukunft hin.

Chercheur postdoctoral – Sensation tactile pour la manipulation dextérieuse

100%, Zurich, durée déterminée

Le Soft Robotics Lab de l'Institute of Robotics and Intelligent Systems de l'ETH Zurich invite les candidats à un poste postdoctoral au sein d'une collaboration de recherche financée par l'industrie. Nous sommes à la recherche d'un chercheur accompli et pratique pour diriger le développement de capteurs tactiles compacts et durables pour les mains robotiques dextérieuses, afin que ces mains puissent manipuler de façon fiable, même lorsque la vision est insuffisante dans des contextes non structurés et réels. Le but de notre laboratoire est de construire, de modéliser et de contrôler des robots d'une manière fondamentalement différente, afin qu'ils deviennent plus flexibles, dextérieux, capables et s'adaptent mieux à leur environnement. Le laboratoire a présenté ses recherches en conception robotique et en algorithmes à travers des applications réelles telles qu'un poisson robotisé pour la locomotion sous-marine et des mains robotiques douces pour la manipulation polyvalente d'objets et de scènes.

Contexte du projet

Les caméras à elles seules ne suffisent pas à une manipulation fiable : l'encombrement, l'occlusion et les objets déformables défavorisent systématiquement les approches basées sur la vision dans des contextes réels. Le sens du toucher comble cette lacune, mais les capteurs tactiles d'aujourd'hui restent en deçà de la compacité, de la durabilité et de la qualité de mesure que les mains robotiques dextérieuses exigent. En tant que chercheur postdoctoral sur ce projet, vous mettrez la détection tactile au centre de la conception de la main plutôt que de la traiter comme une réflexion. S'appuyant sur l'expérience du laboratoire intégrant la détection proprioceptive et tactile dans les mains robotiques musculosquelettiques entraînées par le tendon, vous concevrez, fabriquerez et caractériserez des modules de capteurs qui fournissent des informations de force multi-axes, et conduirez leur intégration dans une plateforme de main de travail.

Description du poste
• Vous dirigerez la conception, la fabrication et la caractérisation de modules compacts de détection tactile qui fournissent des informations de force multi-axes, s'intègrent dans un facteur de forme de main humaine, et restent robustes sous l'usure de manipulations réelles
• Vous étudierez et comparerez différentes modalités de détection tactile, en choisissant les approches les mieux adaptées aux besoins du projet.
• Vous intégrerez les capteurs résultants dans l'une des plates-formes robotisées à tendon du laboratoire, optimisant l'électronique de lecture et l'emballage pour une intégration sans faille du système.
• Vous concevrez des repères représentatifs au niveau des bancs et des tâches et démontrerez les comportements tactiles en boucle fermée pour le contrôle de manipulation en temps réel
• En tant que chercheur principal sur le projet, vous co-superviserez l'étudiant au doctorat et les étudiants de la maîtrise travaillant à vos côtés, prendre en charge la conduite du travail de fin à fin, et diriger la diffusion par la publication dans les meilleurs sites robotiques

Profil

Vous êtes un chercheur accompli qui veut faire une vraie différence avec votre travail Vous êtes très indépendant et affirmé dans la défense de votre direction de recherche, tout en florissant lorsque vous collaborez avec d'autres. Par votre expérience, vous avez idéalement déjà démontré :
• Doctorat en robotique, génie mécanique, mécatronique, génie électrique ou domaine étroitement lié
• Une solide expérience publiée de la recherche matérielle pratique : conception, fabrication et validation expérimentale de systèmes de détection physique ou d'actionnement dans le monde réel
• Expertise démontrée dans au moins une modalité de détection pertinente (tactile, force ou détection optique, par exemple) et confort de travail dans l'électronique, la conception mécanique, la fabrication et le traitement des signaux
• Une expérience de publications évaluées par des pairs dans les principaux sites de robotique qui démontrent à la fois la profondeur technique et la validation des résultats dans le monde réel
• Expérience préalable en mentorat ou en co-supervision d'étudiants au doctorat ou à la maîtrise, et un état d'esprit collaboratif et solidaire
• L'anglais écrit et parlé fort, et le confort de communiquer les résultats à un partenaire de l'industrie ainsi qu'un public académique

jobs.description:
Doctoral position in theoretical modeling of nanocrystal growth

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

The Optical Materials Engineering Laboratory (Prof. David J. Norris) in the Department of Mechanical and Process Engineering (D-MAVT) at ETH Zurich investigates the synthesis, growth, structure, and optical properties of semiconductor nanomaterials. Our interdisciplinary and international team combines materials chemistry, optical spectroscopy, electron microscopy, theoretical modeling, and numerical simulation to understand and control materials at the nanoscale.

Project background

Nanometer-scale semiconductor crystallites exhibit optical properties (e.g., absorption and emission spectra) that are strongly dependent on their size. Because this property is useful for creating tunable optical materials for optoelectronic applications ranging from displays and infrared cameras to nanophotonics and quantum technologies, chemical syntheses have been developed that produce nanocrystals from various semiconductors. The most advanced protocols are those that lead to quasi-spherical particles (known as colloidal quantum dots). However, even state-of-the-art nanocrystal samples contain distributions in particle size and morphology that limit their optical performance.

Two classes of semiconductor nanocrystals have been discovered as exceptions to this rule. They display an unusual form of "discrete" growth, jumping between a series of specific sizes. Semiconductor nanoplatelets can be synthesized with atomically uniform thicknesses, while so-called "magic-sized" nanocrystals grow through a sequence of well-defined sizes. These observations suggest that nanocrystals with exceptionally precise dimensions may be possible. Nevertheless, the mechanisms that govern whether nanoplatelets, magic-sized nanocrystals, or conventional colloidal quantum dots form from a specific synthesis remain poorly understood.

The central aim of this project is to develop a universal theoretical framework that explains how these different nanocrystal growth modes emerge. The resulting understanding will be used to guide experiments toward improved control over nanocrystal size, shape, and optical properties.

Job description

The doctoral student will develop theoretical and computational descriptions of the nucleation and growth of semiconductor nanocrystals. The initial focus will be on combining existing models for CdSe nanoplatelets and magic-sized nanocrystals. The work will subsequently be expanded to include conventional, continuously growing quantum dots and other semiconductor materials, including InP.

The project will combine three complementary modeling approaches: First, the student will use density functional theory (DFT) to calculate the energies of surfactant-terminated nanocrystal surfaces, edges, steps, and vertices. These calculations will provide physically meaningful parameters for the growth models. They will also be used to identify surfactant molecules that may stabilize particular nanocrystal shapes. Second, the student will construct mass-balance models describing the coupled growth and dissolution of nanocrystal populations. These models will examine the competitive growth of nanoplatelets and magic-sized nanocrystals by solving systems of coupled rate equations. The results will be compared directly with experimental stability measurements. The models will then be extended to include quantum dots, with the goal of explaining the transition between discrete and continuous nanocrystal growth. Third, the student will use kinetic Monte Carlo simulations to investigate the early stages of nanocrystal growth. Such calculations will examine how initially small crystallites develop into competing morphologies and how growth conditions influence the selection of nanoplatelets, magic-sized nanocrystals, or quantum dots.

The doctoral student will work closely with experimentalists responsible for nanocrystal synthesis and growth studies. This interaction between theory and experiment is central to the project: experimental results will provide input for the models, while simulations will guide the design of new experiments. The calculations will be performed using ETH Zurich’s high-performance computing infrastructure. In addition to research, the doctoral candidate will contribute to general laboratory activities and will have opportunities to participate in teaching and the supervision of bachelor and master’s students.

Profile

We are seeking a curious, motivated, and self-driven candidate with a strong interest in applying theoretical and computational methods to fundamental problems in materials growth. A strong background in thermodynamics, kinetics, statistical mechanics, solid-state physics, physical chemistry, or materials modeling is expected. Applicants must hold, or be close to completing, an MSc degree in chemistry, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials science, physics, computational science, or a closely related discipline. Experience in one or more of the following areas would be advantageous:
• Density functional theory and electronic-structure calculations
• Kinetic Monte Carlo or other stochastic simulation methods
• Numerical solution of coupled differential or rate equations
• Atomistic or mesoscale modeling of materials
• Semiconductor nanocrystals, surfaces, or colloidal growth
• Scientific programming
• High-performance computing

Prior experience with every method used in the project is not required. The successful candidate should, however, have a strong quantitative foundation and an enthusiasm for learning new computational techniques. Academic excellence, a professional approach to research, and the ability to work independently are expected. The candidate must be able to communicate fluently in English, both orally and in writing, and should enjoy working in a collaborative and international research environment.

We offer

We offer a stimulating doctoral project at the interface of theory, computation, and experiment. The successful candidate will join a collaborative and international research group and will receive training in several complementary approaches to materials modeling. The project provides opportunities for external research collaboration, access to advanced computing facilities, interaction with experimental scientists, participation in international conferences, and the supervision of student research projects.

The position is based in the Department of Mechanical and Process Engineering (D-MAVT) at ETH Zurich’s central campus in Zurich, Switzerland. The student will have access to ETH Zurich’s high-performance computing resources. D-MAVT is an interdisciplinary department encompassing mechanical, process, chemical, and biomedical engineering, as well as robotics and control. ETH Zurich offers an outstanding scientific environment with extensive opportunities for collaboration across materials science, chemistry, physics, and engineering.

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture.
