Assistant Director: in. for the President (m/f/d)

80%-100%, Zurich, permanent

The Executive Board is the strategic and operational centre of ETH Zurich. Under the direction of the President, the school management shapes the future of the university, promotes excellence in teaching and research and strengthens the international positioning. The Executive Board represents ETH Zurich to public authorities, politicians and the public, manages global alliances and maintains close relationships with alumni and supporters.

Job description

As an assistant to our new President, Prof. Dr. Günther Dissertori, you assume responsibility for the professional management of his secretariat and independently and proactively take care of the administrative and organizational tasks. These include:
• Daily Business & Agenda: You are responsible for the smooth daily routine, the planning of a very complex and dynamic agenda and the timely, digital allocation of the documents for the respective meetings
• Interface management: You are the first point of contact for employees, authorities, politics and external stakeholders and ensure accessibility in the secretariat of the President
• Communication & Briefings: Likewise, the independent writing of briefings as well as a perfect correspondence in German and English are part of your tasks.
• Travel Management & Projects: In addition, you work in smaller projects, take over detailed travel preparations and bookings, organize events and events

Profile
• You have several years of experience in a comparable position and bring further training as a directorate assistant with Eidg. professional card or a similar professional background with:
• Contact with various internal and external stakeholders gives you pleasure
• You like to work extremely independently, solution-oriented, forward-thinking and interested in the complex relationships of the processes
• Your experience in organizational/project management can be used profitably in your everyday work
• As part of your tasks, you communicate easily and appropriately in English and German (written and oral), knowledge of French is an advantage
• You have very good knowledge of MS Office, are secure in dealing with various collaboration programs and are open to AI applications
• Absolute reliability, accuracy and discretion are a matter of course for you

We offer

Diversity and sustainability are important to us

In line with our values, ETH Zurich supports an inclusive culture. We promote equal opportunities, value diversity and foster a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all employees and students are respected. On our website on equal opportunities and diversity, you will learn how we ensure a fair and open environment in which everyone can develop and flourish. Sustainability is a key value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future.

Curious? We are too.

We look forward to your online application with the following documents:

• CV

Please apply exclusively via the online application portal. Applications by e-mail or by post will not be considered.

Further information can be found on the ETH Zurich website

For information, Jürg Brunnschweiler, Leiderstab President, juerg.brunnschweiler@sl.ethz.ch, is at your disposal by e-mail (no application documents).

jobs.description:
Doctoral Position: 3D scene reconstruction and multi-modal sensing for digital twins of stone-built heritage

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

The Chair of Geosensors and Engineering Geodesy at ETH Zurich is looking for a Doctoral candidate to work on 3D mapping, scene reconstruction and multi-modal sensing for information-rich digital twins of heritage buildings. The position is part of the collaborative project “HC3 – Heritage Conservation Collaboration Copilots”. HC3 aims to establish information-rich 3D digital twins of stone-built monuments that are interoperable through eXtended Reality (XR), together with the sensing and monitoring methods that provide the data they are built on. These will help us model and understand how stone-built heritage deteriorates, and predict how this deterioration will evolve under climate change. Within the project, you would collaborate with two other Doctoral students employed by the Chair of Physical Chemistry of Building Materials at ETH Zurich and a postdoctoral researcher working on the interface of both Chairs. The HC3 project is lead by Prof. Robert Flatt at Chair of Physical Chemistry of Building Materials and by dr. Tomislav Medic at Chair of Geosensors and Engineering Geodesy (Tomislav would be your direct supervisor).

Job description
• Reality capture at scale: Plan and carry out multi-sensor mapping campaigns of monuments (including LiDAR and imaging technologies using ground-based and UAV platforms)
• Multi-modal data fusion and 3D scene reconstruction: Calibrate, register and fuse point clouds and imagery into unified, data-rich 3D representations (point clouds, meshes, neural radiance fields, 3D Gaussian splatting)
• 3D scene parsing: Develop deep learning enabled methods that segment the scene into individual building elements (stone blocks) for automated digital twin (HBIM) generation
• Inference of material properties: Develop machine learning methods that infer building material properties (stone deterioration type and severity) per element from multi-modal data and time series
• Collaborate on integrating this data into digital twins and extended reality, validate your methods against conservation expert assessments and physical chemistry laboratory experiments; publish in leading journals and conferences; contribute to teaching (upon agreement)

Profile
• MSc degree (completed or about to be completed) in geomatics, remote sensing, computer vision, robotics, computer science or a related field
• Solid background in 2D/3D perception (point cloud and image processing, photogrammetry, 3D reconstruction) and in parameter estimation, incl. machine and deep learning; good programming skills (Python or C++)
• Hands-on experience with laser scanning (LiDAR) or imaging systems is an advantage, and willingness to do fieldwork on monuments is a must
• Further requirements: Interest in interdisciplinary work with material scientists and conservation practitioners; excellent English; French or German is an advantage

We offer

A fully funded four-year doctoral position in an international, dynamic team of highly motivated and supportive colleagues, state-of-the-art sensing equipment, and work on a project with a potential to evolve beyond the initial scope. ETH Zurich offers excellent infrastructure, continuing education and a salary according to ETH regulations, in a city with outstanding quality of life.

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:
• CV, including a list of publications (if applicable)
• Cover Letter, including the following two elements: A brief description (max. 1/2 A4 page + 1 figure) of a result from your previous work that you are proud of and presents relevant skills for this project and a brief description (max. 1/2 A4 page) of your vision of your Doctoral research project
• Names and contact information of two references
• Copy of your MSc degree/diploma

Further information about the Department (D-BAUG), the Institute (IGP), and the Research group (GSEG) can be found on our websites: DBAUG , IGP , GSEG . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Tomislav Medic , tmedic@ethz.ch (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

About ETH Zürich

ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

descriptionByLocale.it:
Posizione Dottorale: ricostruzione della scena 3D e rilevamento multimodale per gemelli digitali del patrimonio in pietra

100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato

La Cattedra di Geosensori e Engineering Geodesy dell'ETH di Zurigo sta cercando un Dottorato candidato per lavorare su mappatura 3D, ricostruzione della scena e rilevamento multi-modale per gemelli digitali ricchi di informazioni di edifici di patrimonio. La posizione è parte del progetto collaborativo “HC3 – Heritage Conservation Collaboration Copilots”. HC3 mira a stabilire gemelle digitali 3D ricche di informazioni di monumenti costruiti in pietra che sono interoperabili attraverso la realtà eXtended (XR), insieme ai metodi di rilevamento e monitoraggio che forniscono i dati su cui sono costruiti. Questi ci aiuteranno a modellare e capire come il patrimonio costruito in pietra si deteriora, e prevedere come questo deterioramento si evolverà sotto il cambiamento climatico. All'interno del progetto, collaborerai con altri due dottorandi impiegati dalla Cattedra di Chimica Fisica dei Materiali Edili dell'ETH di Zurigo e da un ricercatore post-dottorato che lavora sull'interfaccia di entrambe le Sedie. Il progetto HC3 è guidato dal Prof. Robert Flatt a Chair of Physical Chemistry of Building Materials e dal dr. Tomislav Medic a Chair of Geosensors and Engineering Geodesy (Tomislav sarebbe il vostro supervisore diretto).

Descrizione del lavoro
• Acquisizione della realtà in scala: Pianifica e realizza campagne di mappatura multisensoriale di monumenti (tra cui le tecnologie LiDAR e imaging utilizzando piattaforme UAV e terrestri)
• Multi-modal data fusion e ricostruzione della scena 3D: calibrare, registrare e fondere le nubi del punto e le immagini in rappresentazioni 3D unificate e ricche di dati (nubi punto, mesh, campi di radianza neurale, 3D Gaussian splatting)
• Parasing della scena 3D: Sviluppare metodi di deep learning abilitati che segmentano la scena in singoli elementi di costruzione (blocchi di pietra) per la generazione automatizzata dei gemelli digitali (HBIM)
• Inferenza delle proprietà materiali: Sviluppare metodi di apprendimento automatico che inferiscono le proprietà dei materiali da costruzione (tipo di deterioramento della pietra e gravità) per elemento da dati multimodali e serie temporali
• Collaborare per integrare questi dati in gemelli digitali e realtà estesa, convalidare i vostri metodi contro le valutazioni di esperti di conservazione e gli esperimenti di laboratorio di chimica fisica; pubblicare in riviste e conferenze principali; contribuire all'insegnamento (su accordo)

Profilo
• Grado MSc (completo o in procinto di essere completato) in geomatica, telerilevamento, visione del computer, robotica, informatica o un campo correlato
• Sfondo solido nella percezione 2D/3D (elaborazione punto cloud e immagine, fotogrammetria, ricostruzione 3D) e nella stima dei parametri, inclusa la macchina e l'apprendimento profondo; buone capacità di programmazione (Python o C++)
• Esperienza pratica con scansione laser (LiDAR) o sistemi di imaging è un vantaggio, e la volontà di fare lavori sul campo su monumenti è un must
• Ulteriori requisiti: Interesse nel lavoro interdisciplinare con scienziati materiali e professionisti della conservazione; inglese eccellente; francese o tedesco è un vantaggio

Offriamo

Una posizione di dottorato di quattro anni completamente finanziata in un team internazionale e dinamico di colleghi altamente motivati e di supporto, apparecchiature di rilevamento all'avanguardia, e lavorare su un progetto con un potenziale per evolversi oltre il campo iniziale. ETH Zurich offre eccellenti infrastrutture, formazione continua e uno stipendio secondo le normative ETH, in una città con eccezionale qualità di vita.

Apprezziamo la diversità e la sostenibilità

In linea con i nostri valori, ETH Zurich incoraggia una cultura inclusiva. Promuoviamo l'uguaglianza di opportunità, la diversità di valore e nutrire un ambiente di lavoro e di apprendimento in cui i diritti e la dignità di tutto il nostro staff e gli studenti sono rispettati. Visita il nostro sito web Equal Opportunities and Diversity per scoprire come garantiamo un ambiente equo e aperto che permetta a tutti di crescere e fiorire. La sostenibilità è un valore fondamentale per noi – stiamo costantemente lavorando verso un futuro neutro dal clima.

Curioso? Anche noi.

Non vediamo l'ora di ricevere la tua domanda online con i seguenti documenti:
• CV, incluso un elenco di pubblicazioni (se applicabile)
• Lettera di copertina, compresi i seguenti due elementi: Una breve descrizione (max. 1/2 A4 pagina + 1 cifra) di un risultato dal vostro lavoro precedente che siete orgogliosi e presenta competenze rilevanti per questo progetto e una breve descrizione (max. 1/2 A4 pagina) della vostra visione del vostro progetto di ricerca di dottorato
• Nomi e informazioni di contatto di due riferimenti
• Copia del diploma MSc/diploma

Ulteriori informazioni sul Dipartimento (D-BAUG), l'Istituto (IGP), e il gruppo di ricerca (GSEG) possono essere trovati sui nostri siti web: DBAUG , IGP , GSEG . Le domande relative alla posizione devono essere indirizzate a Tomislav Medic , tmedic@ethz.ch (nessuna domanda).

Si prega di notare che accettiamo esclusivamente le applicazioni inviate tramite il nostro portale di applicazioni online. Le applicazioni via e-mail o servizi postali non saranno considerate.

Vorremmo sottolineare che la pre-selezione è effettuata dai reclutatori responsabili e non dall'intelligenza artificiale.

Informazioni su ETH Zürich

ETH Zurich è una delle università più importanti del mondo specializzata in
scienza e tecnologia. Siamo rinomati per la nostra eccellente educazione,
ricerca fondamentale all'avanguardia e trasferimento diretto di nuove conoscenze
nella società. Oltre 30.000 persone provenienti da più di 120 paesi
università per essere un luogo che promuove il pensiero indipendente e un
ambiente che ispira eccellenza. Situato nel cuore dell'Europa,
ancora forgiando connessioni in tutto il mondo, lavoriamo insieme a
sviluppare soluzioni per le sfide globali di oggi e domani.

Der Lehrstuhl für Geosensorik und Ingenieurgeodäsie der ETH Zürich sucht einen Doktoranden, der sich mit 3D-Mapping, Szenenrekonstruktion und multimodaler Sensorik für informationsreiche digitale Zwillinge von historischen Gebäuden beschäftigt. Die Position ist Teil des Verbundprojekts „HC3 – Heritage Conservation Collaboration Copilots. HC3 zielt darauf ab, informationsreiche digitale 3D-Zwillinge von Steindenkmälern zu etablieren, die durch eXtended Reality (XR) interoperabel sind, zusammen mit den Erfassungs- und Überwachungsmethoden, die die Daten liefern, auf denen sie aufgebaut sind. Diese werden uns helfen zu modellieren und zu verstehen, wie sich das steinerne Erbe verschlechtert und wie sich diese Verschlechterung unter dem Klimawandel entwickeln wird. Im Rahmen des Projekts arbeiten Sie mit zwei weiteren Doktorandinnen und Doktoranden des Lehrstuhls für Physikalische Chemie von Baustoffen der ETH Zürich und einem Postdoktoranden zusammen, der an der Schnittstelle beider Lehrstühle arbeitet. Das HC3-Projekt wird von Prof. Robert Flatt am Lehrstuhl für Physikalische Chemie von Baustoffen und von Dr. Tomislav Medic am Lehrstuhl für Geosensoren und Ingenieurgeodäsie (Tomislav wäre Ihr direkter Vorgesetzter).

Stellenbeschreibung
• Realitätserfassung in großem Maßstab: Planung und Durchführung von Multisensor-Mapping-Kampagnen von Denkmälern (einschließlich LiDAR- und Bildgebungstechnologien mit bodengestützten und UAV-Plattformen)
• Multimodale Datenfusion und 3D-Szenenrekonstruktion: kalibrieren, registrieren und verschmelzen Punktwolken und Bilder in einheitliche, datenreiche 3D-Darstellungen (Punktwolken, Maschen, neuronale Strahlungsfelder, 3D-Gauß-Splatting)
• 3D-Szenen-Parsing: Entwicklung von Deep Learning-fähigen Methoden, die die Szene in einzelne Bausteine (Steinblöcke) für die automatisierte digitale Zwillingsgeneration (HBIM) segmentieren
• Schlussfolgerung von Materialeigenschaften: Entwicklung von Methoden des maschinellen Lernens, die aus multimodalen Daten und Zeitreihen auf Baumaterialeigenschaften (Steinverschlechterungsart und Schweregrad) pro Element schließen
• Arbeiten Sie an der Integration dieser Daten in digitale Zwillinge und erweiterte Realität, validieren Sie Ihre Methoden gegen Experteneinschätzungen zur Erhaltung und physikalische Chemie Laborexperimente; veröffentlichen Sie in führenden Zeitschriften und Konferenzen; tragen Sie zur Lehre bei (nach Vereinbarung)

Profil
• MSc-Abschluss (abgeschlossen oder kurz vor dem Abschluss) in Geomatik, Fernerkundung, Computer Vision, Robotik, Informatik oder einem verwandten Bereich
• Solider Hintergrund in der 2D/3D-Wahrnehmung (Punktwolken- und Bildverarbeitung, Photogrammetrie, 3D-Rekonstruktion) und in der Parameterschätzung, inkl. maschinellem und Deep Learning; gute Programmierkenntnisse (Python oder C++)
• Praktische Erfahrung mit Laserscanning (LiDAR) oder Bildgebungssystemen ist von Vorteil, und die Bereitschaft, Feldforschung an Denkmälern durchzuführen, ist ein Muss
• Weitere Voraussetzungen: Interesse an interdisziplinärer Arbeit mit Materialwissenschaftlern und Konservatoren; exzellentes Englisch; Französisch oder Deutsch ist von Vorteil

Wir bieten

Eine vollständig finanzierte vierjährige Doktorandenstelle in einem internationalen, dynamischen Team von hochmotivierten und unterstützenden Kollegen, modernste Sensorik und Arbeit an einem Projekt, das sich über den ursprünglichen Rahmen hinaus entwickeln kann. Die ETH Zürich bietet exzellente Infrastruktur, Weiterbildung und ein Gehalt nach ETH-Vorschriften in einer Stadt mit herausragender Lebensqualität.

Wir legen Wert auf Vielfalt und Nachhaltigkeit

Im Einklang mit unseren Werten fördert die ETH Zürich eine inklusive Kultur. Wir fördern Chancengleichheit, schätzen Vielfalt und fördern ein Arbeits- und Lernumfeld, in dem die Rechte und die Würde aller unserer Mitarbeiter und Studenten respektiert werden. Besuchen Sie unsere Website für Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt, um herauszufinden, wie wir ein faires und offenes Umfeld gewährleisten, in dem jeder wachsen und gedeihen kann. Nachhaltigkeit ist für uns ein zentraler Wert – wir arbeiten konsequent auf eine klimaneutrale Zukunft hin.

descriptionByLocale.fr:
Position doctorale: reconstruction de la scène 3D et détection multimodale pour jumeaux numériques du patrimoine en pierre

100%, Zurich, durée déterminée

Le président de Geosensors and Engineering Geodesy à l'ETH Zurich est à la recherche d'un candidat au doctorat pour travailler sur la cartographie 3D, la reconstruction des scènes et la détection multimodale pour les jumeaux numériques riches en information des bâtiments patrimoniaux. Le poste fait partie du projet de collaboration «HC3 – Heritage Conservation Collaboration Copilots». HC3 vise à établir des jumelles numériques 3D riches en informations de monuments en pierre qui sont interopérables par eXtended Reality (XR), ainsi que les méthodes de détection et de surveillance qui fournissent les données sur lesquelles ils sont basés. Ils nous aideront à modéliser et à comprendre comment le patrimoine bâti en pierre se détériore et à prédire comment cette détérioration évoluera sous le changement climatique. Dans le cadre du projet, vous collaboreriez avec deux autres étudiants au doctorat employés par la Chaire de chimie physique des matériaux de construction à l'ETH Zurich et un chercheur postdoctoral travaillant sur l'interface des deux chaires. Le projet HC3 est dirigé par le Prof. Robert Flatt à la chaire de chimie physique des matériaux de construction et par le Dr Tomislav Medic à la chaire de géosenseurs et de géodésie (Tomislav serait votre superviseur direct).

Description du poste
• Capture de la réalité à l'échelle : Planifier et réaliser des campagnes de cartographie multicapteurs des monuments (y compris le LiDAR et les technologies d'imagerie utilisant des plates-formes terrestres et UAV)
• Fusion de données multimodale et reconstruction de la scène 3D : Calibrer, enregistrer et fusionner des nuages et des images de points en représentations 3D unifiées et riches en données (nuages de points, maillages, champs de rayonnement neuronal, stratification gaussienne 3D)
• Analyse de la scène 3D : Développer des méthodes d'apprentissage profond permettant de segmenter la scène en éléments de construction individuels (pierres) pour la génération de jumeaux numériques automatisés (HBIM)
• Inférence des propriétés des matériaux : Développer des méthodes d'apprentissage automatique qui permettent d'inférer les propriétés des matériaux de construction (type et gravité de la détérioration des pierres) par élément à partir de données multimodales et de séries chronologiques
• Collaborer à l'intégration de ces données dans les jumelles numériques et la réalité étendue, valider vos méthodes à l'aide d'évaluations d'experts en conservation et d'expériences de laboratoire en chimie physique; publier dans des revues et des conférences de pointe; contribuer à l'enseignement (sur accord)

Profil
• Maîtrise en géomatique, télédétection, vision informatique, robotique, informatique ou domaine connexe
• Fond solide dans la perception 2D/3D (traitement des nuages et des images, photogrammétrie, reconstruction 3D) et dans l'estimation des paramètres, y compris la machine et l'apprentissage profond; bonnes compétences en programmation (Python ou C++)
• L'expérience pratique avec le balayage laser (LiDAR) ou les systèmes d'imagerie est un avantage, et la volonté de faire des travaux de terrain sur les monuments est un must
• Autres exigences: Intérêt pour le travail interdisciplinaire avec les scientifiques du matériel et les praticiens de la conservation; excellent anglais; français ou allemand est un avantage

Nous offrons

Un doctorat de quatre ans entièrement financé au sein d'une équipe internationale dynamique composée de collègues très motivés et solidaires, d'équipement de détection de pointe et de travail sur un projet susceptible d'évoluer au-delà de la portée initiale. L'ETH Zurich offre une excellente infrastructure, une formation continue et un salaire selon la réglementation de l'ETH, dans une ville avec une qualité de vie exceptionnelle.

Nous apprécions la diversité et la durabilité

Conformément à nos valeurs , ETH Zurich encourage une culture inclusive. Nous favorisons l'égalité des chances, valorisons la diversité et favorisons un environnement de travail et d'apprentissage dans lequel les droits et la dignité de tous nos employés et étudiants sont respectés. Visitez notre site Web sur l'égalité des chances et la diversité pour découvrir comment nous garantissons un environnement équitable et ouvert qui permet à chacun de grandir et de prospérer. La durabilité est une valeur fondamentale pour nous – nous travaillons constamment vers un avenir neutre sur le plan climatique.

Curieux ? Nous aussi.

Nous sommes impatients de recevoir votre demande en ligne avec les documents suivants :
• CV, y compris une liste de publications (le cas échéant)
• Lettre de présentation, comprenant les deux éléments suivants : Une brève description (max. 1/2 A4 page + 1 figure) d'un résultat de votre travail précédent dont vous êtes fier et présente des compétences pertinentes pour ce projet et une brève description (max. 1/2 A4 page) de votre vision de votre projet de recherche au doctorat
• Noms et coordonnées de deux références
• Copie de votre diplôme/diplôme de maîtrise

De plus amples informations sur le Département (D-BAUG), l'Institut (IGP) et le Groupe de recherche (GSEG) sont disponibles sur nos sites web: DBAUG , IGP , GSEG . Les questions concernant le poste doivent être adressées à Tomislav Medic , tmedic@ethz.ch (aucune demande).

Veuillez noter que nous acceptons exclusivement les demandes soumises par notre portail en ligne. Les demandes par courriel ou par la poste ne seront pas prises en considération.

Nous tenons à souligner que la présélection est effectuée par les recruteurs responsables et non par l'intelligence artificielle.

A propos de l'ETH Zürich

ETH Zurich est l'une des plus grandes universités du monde spécialisées dans
la science et la technologie. Nous sommes réputés pour notre excellente éducation,
recherche fondamentale de pointe et transfert direct de nouvelles connaissances
dans la société. Plus de 30 000 personnes de plus de 120 pays trouvent notre
l'université d'être un lieu qui favorise la pensée indépendante et un
environnement qui inspire l'excellence. Situé au cœur de l'Europe,
mais forgeant des liens partout dans le monde, nous travaillons ensemble pour
développer des solutions aux défis mondiaux d'aujourd'hui et de demain.

Die Abteilung Procurement Services VPIN ist für die Beschaffung der Bereiche Bau, Infrastruktur, Betrieb und ICT verantwortlich - wirtschaftlich, rechtskonform und nachhaltig. Für den Ausbau unserer Einkaufsorganisation suchen wir eine Einkaufspersönlichkeit, die anspruchsvolle Beschaffungen eigenverantwortlich umsetzt und sich gerne in neue Themen einarbeitet.

Gestalten Sie als strategische:r Einkäufer:in mit uns eine vielseitige Beschaffung und entwickeln Sie den Einkauf der ETH Zürich weiter.

Stellenbeschreibung

In dieser Funktion übernehmen Sie eigenverantwortlich Beschaffungsvorhaben entlang des gesamten Beschaffungsprozesses. Sie führen Vergaben von freihändigen Verfahren bis hin zu öffentlichen Ausschreibungen im Staatsvertragsbereich durch und begleiten diese von der Bedarfsanalyse über die Ausschreibung und Evaluation bis zum Vertragsabschluss. Dabei beschaffen Sie vielfältige Dienstleistungen und Güter im Infrastrukturumfeld, analysieren Märkte und entwickeln gemeinsam mit den Fachbereichen geeignete Beschaffungswege.

Als kompetente:r Ansprechpartner:in beraten Sie interne Auftraggebende bei der Definition ihrer Anforderungen, erarbeiten aussagekräftige Leistungsbeschreibungen sowie Eignungs- und Zuschlagskriterien und sorgen dafür, dass fachliche, wirtschaftliche und rechtliche Anforderungen optimal miteinander verbunden werden. Zudem entwickeln Sie Beschaffungsstrategien und Rahmenverträge weiter, identifizieren Bündelungspotenziale und berücksichtigen dabei Qualität, Risiken, Nachhaltigkeit und Lebenszykluskosten.

Gemeinsam mit Fachstellen und dem Rechtsdienst gestalten Sie Verträge und Lieferantenbeziehungen aktiv mit, klären kommerzielle Fragestellungen und unterstützen Verhandlungen sowie Angebotsbereinigungen. Darüber hinaus bringen Sie Ihre Expertise in die Weiterentwicklung des Einkaufs ein, fördern effiziente Prozesse und digitale Arbeitsweisen und tragen mit Ihrem Wissen zu einer erfolgreichen Zusammenarbeit mit den Fachabteilungen bei.

Profil

• Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im strategischen Einkauf sowie in der Durchführung öffentlicher Beschaffungsverfahren

• Erfahrung in der Beschaffung von Dienstleistungen und im Erstellen aussagekräftiger Ausschreibungsunterlagen
• Analytisches Denkvermögen sowie ein hohes Mass an Wirtschafts- und Prozessverständnis
• Strukturierte, selbstständige Arbeitsweise mit ausgeprägter Organisationsfähigkeit
• Kommunikationsstärke, Verhandlungsgeschick und Freude an der Zusammenarbeit mit unterschiedlichen Anspruchsgruppen
• Erfahrung im Infrastruktur-, Bau-, Planungs- oder Facility-Management-Umfeld von Vorteil
• Sehr gute Deutsch- und gute Englischkenntnisse
• Hohe Affinität zu digitalen Arbeitsweisen sowie zu Einkaufs- und Vergabeplattformen

Wir bieten

Ihr Beruf mit Wirkung: Werden Sie Teil der ETH Zürich, die nicht nur Ihre berufliche Entwicklung unterstützt, sondern auch aktiv zu positiven Veränderungen in der Gesellschaft beiträgt.

Arbeiten beim Vizepräsidium für Infrastruktur und Nachhaltigkeit (VPIN) bedeutet, die Zukunft der ETH Zürich aktiv mitzugestalten - eine inspirierende, internationale und innovative Institution. Ihr Engagement schafft beste Voraussetzungen für Exzellenz in Lehre, Forschung, Wissenstransfer und Nachhaltigkeit der ETH Zürich.

In einer offenen, inspirierenden Atmosphäre bilden Vertrauen, Verlässlichkeit und gegenseitiger Respekt das Fundament unserer Zusammenarbeit. Wir bieten Ihnen nicht nur Sicherheit, sondern auch vielfältige Weiterentwicklungsmöglichkeiten. Bei uns erwartet Sie eine sinnstiftende Arbeit in einem innovativen und wertschätzenden Umfeld, das Sie mitgestalten können und das Ihnen neue Perspektiven eröffnet.

80%-100%, Zurigo, permanente

L'ETH Zurigo è una delle principali università del mondo nella ricerca e nell'insegnamento. Il dipartimento Procurement Services VPIN è responsabile per l'approvvigionamento delle aree di costruzione, infrastruttura, funzionamento e ICT - economico, legalmente conforme e sostenibile. Per l'espansione della nostra organizzazione di acquisto, siamo alla ricerca di una persona di acquisto che implementa gli appalti esigenti in modo indipendente e ama familiarizzare con nuovi argomenti.

Come acquirente strategico, progettare acquisti versatili con noi e sviluppare ulteriormente gli appalti presso ETH Zurich.

Descrizione del lavoro

In questa funzione, si assume la responsabilità di progetti di approvvigionamento lungo l'intero processo di approvvigionamento. Effettuano premi che vanno dalle procedure di concessione diretta alle offerte pubbliche nel settore dei contratti di stato e li accompagnano da analisi delle esigenze all'offerta e valutazione alla conclusione dei contratti. In questo modo, si fornisce una vasta gamma di servizi e merci nell'ambiente delle infrastrutture, analizzare i mercati e sviluppare percorsi di approvvigionamento adeguati insieme alle aree specializzate.

Come persona di contatto competente, si consiglia ai clienti interni sulla definizione dei loro requisiti, sviluppare descrizioni dei servizi significativi, nonché criteri di idoneità e di riconoscimento e garantire che i requisiti professionali, economici e legali sono combinati in modo ottimale. Inoltre, svilupperai ulteriormente le strategie di approvvigionamento e gli accordi quadro, identificherai le potenzialità di bundling, tenendo conto della qualità, dei rischi, della sostenibilità e dei costi del ciclo di vita.

Insieme con gli uffici specializzati e il servizio legale, si plasmano attivamente contratti e rapporti di fornitori, chiariscono le questioni commerciali e supportano i negoziati e gli adattamenti delle offerte. Inoltre, si contribuisce alla vostra esperienza per l'ulteriore sviluppo di acquisto, promuovere processi efficienti e metodi di lavoro digitali e contribuire con la vostra conoscenza ad una collaborazione di successo con i dipartimenti specializzati.

Profilo
• Istruzione superiore (HF, FH o università) in amministrazione aziendale, ingegneria, diritto, gestione della supply chain o una specializzazione comparabile; formazione alternativa ulteriore nell'acquisto a livello di carta professionale o diploma
• Diversi anni di esperienza professionale nell'acquisto strategico e nell'attuazione delle procedure di appalti pubblici
• Conoscenza approfondita della legge sugli appalti svizzeri (BöB/VöB o IVöB)
• Esperienza nei servizi e produzione di documenti di gara significativi
• competenze di pensiero analitico e un alto grado di comprensione economica e di processo
• Metodi di lavoro strutturati e indipendenti con forte capacità organizzativa
• La forza della comunicazione, le capacità di negoziazione e il godimento di lavorare con diversi stakeholder
• L'esperienza nell'infrastruttura, nell'edilizia, nella pianificazione o nell'ambiente di gestione delle strutture è vantaggiosa
• Molto buone competenze in tedesco e inglese
• Alta affinità per i metodi di lavoro digitali e per le piattaforme di acquisto e di approvvigionamento

Offriamo

Entra a far parte dell'ETH di Zurigo, che non solo supporta il tuo sviluppo professionale, ma contribuisce attivamente ai cambiamenti positivi nella società.

Lavorare per il Vice Presidente delle Infrastrutture e Sostenibilità (VPIN) significa plasmare attivamente il futuro dell'ETH Zurigo – un'istituzione ispiratrice, internazionale e innovativa. Il loro impegno crea le migliori condizioni per l'eccellenza nell'insegnamento, nella ricerca, nel trasferimento delle conoscenze e nella sostenibilità dell'ETH Zurigo.

In un'atmosfera aperta e stimolante, fiducia, affidabilità e rispetto reciproco costituiscono la base della nostra cooperazione. Non solo vi offriamo la sicurezza, ma anche una vasta gamma di ulteriori opportunità di sviluppo. Con noi, ci si può aspettare un lavoro significativo in un ambiente innovativo e apprezzativo che si può aiutare a modellare e che apre nuove prospettive.
• All'ETH di Zurigo ci si può aspettare un ambiente dinamico e internazionale.
• C'è spazio per soluzioni pratiche e creative e pratiche sono molto benvenuti
• Viviamo: Apprendimento permanente
• Sconti come abbonamenti di trasporto pubblico e condivisione di auto, ampia offerta sportiva dell'ASVZ, assistenza per bambini, servizi pensionistici attraenti, ecc.

La diversità e la sostenibilità sono importanti per noi

In linea con i nostri valori, ETH Zurich supporta una cultura inclusiva. Promuoviamo pari opportunità, la diversità del valore e coltiviamo un ambiente di lavoro e di apprendimento che rispetta i diritti e la dignità di tutti i dipendenti e gli studenti. Sul nostro sito web su pari opportunità e diversità, imparerai come garantiamo un ambiente equo e aperto in cui tutti possono svilupparsi e prosperare. La sostenibilità è un valore fondamentale per noi – stiamo costantemente lavorando verso un futuro neutro dal clima.

Curioso? Anche noi.

• CVC
• Certificati di occupazione
• Diploma rilevanti

jobs.description:
Teaching and Research Assistant (3 positions)

40%, Zurich, fixed-term

The Department of Architecture (D-ARCH) at ETH Zurich is among the world’s leading schools of architecture, known for its teaching as much as for its research. The Chair of Architectural Behaviorology, led by Prof. Momoyo Kaijima, is looking for new members to join its team. The following positions are open:
• Teaching Assistant, 40%, starting January 2027
• Research Assistant, 40%, starting January 2027
• Teaching Assistant, 40%, starting August 2027

Project background

Since 2017, the Chair of Architectural Behaviorology has been investigating architectural form through the lens of behaviors: the behavior of climate and materials, of humans and non-humans, and of architectural typologies. This approach aims to understand architecture within ecological networks, creating better accessibility to resources and finding shared commons. We see practice, research, and education as one integrated, cyclical activity in which theory and practice inform and shape one another.

Because architecture is grounded in specific places, we explore its relationship to regional lifestyles, including urban, mountainous, and agricultural contexts. In doing so, we address gaps in architectural discourse, particularly the divide between areas of consumption and production.

Our research projects include, for example, Swiss Window Journey , a study of window typologies across Switzerland, or Valley Section , a study of Swiss industrial heritage through territorial cross-sections. We also work on Housing, Shelter, and Care Behaviorology, which address domestic, post-disaster, and healthcare environments. Together with other ETH chairs, we have developed structural and spatial experiments rooted in Behaviorology.

In teaching, the Chair leads a second-year Design Studio, where around 70 students are introduced to the methodologies of Architectural Behaviorology and Actor Network Theory, as tools both for designing architecture and for understanding our built, lived, and social environment. Students gain hands-on experience in designing and drawing architectural projects, doing research, working in teams, building 1:1 structures, and presenting and defending their ideas.

You can find more information about the chair and the students’ work on our website .

Job description

As a teaching assistant (40%), you teach a combination of architectural design and research within the framework of Architectural Behaviorology. You understand students' ideas and help them develop their projects further. Your knowledge of structure, construction, and detailing lets you support them in these matters too, and your research-based thinking helps them find good, workable solutions to design problems. Studio days are Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Your tasks include:
• Preparation of materials and documents for the design studio
• Supporting the students in developing their projects
• Evaluating and grading student projects
• Holding short input lectures and workshops for the studio

As a research assistant (40%), you conduct research within the framework of Architectural Behaviorology. You work across a broad range of ongoing research projects on Window Behaviorology, Urban-Rural Commons, Housing in Switzerland, Architecture for Care, and others. Among other tasks, you organize workshops and seminar weeks, help edit and publish books, and arrange exhibitions.

Teaching and research assistant contracts are limited to one year, and can be renewed annually for up to 6 years.

Profile

You have
• A master’s degree in architecture
• Good knowledge of English and (Swiss) German: the design studios and research are mostly taught and led in English, while German is needed to work with local collaborators
• Solid knowledge of the Swiss architectural landscape, including construction, detailing, and the most common regulations
• A good understanding of architectural design practice, and of Swiss socio-economic, cultural, historical, and political context
• Residence in Switzerland, ideally in the Zurich area

Ideally, you also have
• 2-3 years of professional experience, including work on execution plans
• Knowledge of French or Italian

We offer
• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society
• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents, written in English:
• CV (max. 1 page)
• Portfolio with examples of your architectural work and research (max. 10 pages)
• Cover letter explaining your motivation and your interest in joining the Chair of Architectural Behaviorology (max. 1 page)

Further information about Department of Architecture can be found on our Website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Samuel Dayer at dayer@arch.ethz.ch (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

The application deadline is 22 November 2026.

Insegnamento e Ricerca Assistente (3 posizioni)

40%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato

Il Dipartimento di Architettura (D-ARCH) dell’ETH di Zurigo è tra le principali scuole di architettura del mondo, note per il suo insegnamento tanto quanto per la sua ricerca. La Cattedra di Comportamento Architettonico, guidata dal Prof. Momoyo Kaijima, sta cercando nuovi membri per unirsi alla sua squadra. Le seguenti posizioni sono aperte:
• Insegnante, 40%, a partire dal gennaio 2027
• Ricerca Assistente, 40%, a partire dal gennaio 2027
• Insegnante, 40%, a partire da agosto 2027

Sfondo del progetto

Dal 2017, la Cattedra di Comportamento Architettonico sta indagando sulla forma architettonica attraverso la lente dei comportamenti: il comportamento del clima e dei materiali, degli esseri umani e dei non umani e delle tipologie architettoniche. Questo approccio mira a comprendere l'architettura all'interno di reti ecologiche, creando una migliore accessibilità alle risorse e trovando comuni condivisi. Vediamo la pratica, la ricerca e l'istruzione come un'attività ciclica integrata in cui la teoria e la pratica si informano e si modellano a vicenda.

Poiché l'architettura è fondata in luoghi specifici, esploriamo il suo rapporto con gli stili di vita regionali, compresi i contesti urbani, montagnosi e agricoli. In questo modo, affrontiamo lacune nel discorso architettonico, in particolare la divisione tra aree di consumo e produzione.

I nostri progetti di ricerca includono, ad esempio, Swiss Window Journey , uno studio sulle tipologie di finestre in tutta la Svizzera, o Valley Section , uno studio del patrimonio industriale svizzero attraverso sezioni territoriali. Lavoriamo anche su Housing, Shelter e Care Behaviorology, che affrontano ambienti domestici, post-disaster e sanitari. Insieme ad altre sedie ETH, abbiamo sviluppato esperimenti strutturali e spaziali radicati nella Behaviorologia.

Nell'insegnamento, la Cattedra conduce un secondo anno Design Studio, dove circa 70 studenti sono presentati alle metodologie della Teoria di Comportamento Architettonico e Rete Attore, come strumenti sia per la progettazione dell'architettura che per la comprensione del nostro costruito, vissuto e ambiente sociale. Gli studenti acquisiscono esperienza pratica nella progettazione e nel disegno di progetti architettonici, facendo ricerca, lavorando in team, costruendo strutture 1:1, e presentando e difendendo le loro idee.

Potete trovare ulteriori informazioni sulla sedia e sul lavoro degli studenti sul nostro sito web .

Descrizione del lavoro

Come assistente di insegnamento (40%), si insegna una combinazione di progettazione architettonica e di ricerca nel quadro della Behaviorologia Architettonica. Capisci le idee degli studenti e aiutali a sviluppare ulteriormente i loro progetti. La vostra conoscenza della struttura, della costruzione e del dettaglio consente di supportarli anche in queste questioni, e il vostro pensiero basato sulla ricerca li aiuta a trovare soluzioni buone e lavorabili per i problemi di progettazione. I giorni di studio sono martedì e mercoledì. I vostri compiti includono:
• Preparazione di materiali e documenti per lo studio di progettazione
• Sostenere gli studenti nello sviluppo dei loro progetti
• Valutazione e valutazione dei progetti studenteschi
• Tenere brevi lezioni di input e workshop per lo studio

Come assistente di ricerca (40%), si conduce la ricerca nel quadro della Behaviorologia Architettonica. Lavori in una vasta gamma di progetti di ricerca in corso su Window Behaviorology, Urban-Rural Commons, Housing in Svizzera, Architecture for Care e altri. Tra le altre attività, si organizzano workshop e settimane di seminario, aiutare a modificare e pubblicare libri, e organizzare mostre.

I contratti di insegnamento e di assistente di ricerca sono limitati ad un anno, e possono essere rinnovati annualmente fino a 6 anni.

Profilo

Tu hai

• Conoscenza solida del paesaggio architettonico svizzero, tra cui la costruzione, il dettaglio e le normative più comuni

descriptionByLocale.en:
Teaching and Research Assistant (3 positions)

40%, Zurich, fixed-term

The Department of Architecture (D-ARCH) at ETH Zurich is among the world’s leading schools of architecture, known for its teaching as much as for its research. The Chair of Architectural Behaviorology, led by Prof. Momoyo Kaijima, is looking for new members to join its team. The following positions are open:
• Teaching Assistant, 40%, starting January 2027
• Research Assistant, 40%, starting January 2027
• Teaching Assistant, 40%, starting August 2027

Project background

Since 2017, the Chair of Architectural Behaviorology has been investigating architectural form through the lens of behaviors: the behavior of climate and materials, of humans and non-humans, and of architectural typologies. This approach aims to understand architecture within ecological networks, creating better accessibility to resources and finding shared commons. We see practice, research, and education as one integrated, cyclical activity in which theory and practice inform and shape one another.

Because architecture is grounded in specific places, we explore its relationship to regional lifestyles, including urban, mountainous, and agricultural contexts. In doing so, we address gaps in architectural discourse, particularly the divide between areas of consumption and production.

Our research projects include, for example, Swiss Window Journey , a study of window typologies across Switzerland, or Valley Section , a study of Swiss industrial heritage through territorial cross-sections. We also work on Housing, Shelter, and Care Behaviorology, which address domestic, post-disaster, and healthcare environments. Together with other ETH chairs, we have developed structural and spatial experiments rooted in Behaviorology.

In teaching, the Chair leads a second-year Design Studio, where around 70 students are introduced to the methodologies of Architectural Behaviorology and Actor Network Theory, as tools both for designing architecture and for understanding our built, lived, and social environment. Students gain hands-on experience in designing and drawing architectural projects, doing research, working in teams, building 1:1 structures, and presenting and defending their ideas.

You can find more information about the chair and the students’ work on our website .

Job description

As a teaching assistant (40%), you teach a combination of architectural design and research within the framework of Architectural Behaviorology. You understand students' ideas and help them develop their projects further. Your knowledge of structure, construction, and detailing lets you support them in these matters too, and your research-based thinking helps them find good, workable solutions to design problems. Studio days are Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Your tasks include:
• Preparation of materials and documents for the design studio
• Supporting the students in developing their projects
• Evaluating and grading student projects
• Holding short input lectures and workshops for the studio

As a research assistant (40%), you conduct research within the framework of Architectural Behaviorology. You work across a broad range of ongoing research projects on Window Behaviorology, Urban-Rural Commons, Housing in Switzerland, Architecture for Care, and others. Among other tasks, you organize workshops and seminar weeks, help edit and publish books, and arrange exhibitions.

Teaching and research assistant contracts are limited to one year, and can be renewed annually for up to 6 years.

Profile

You have
• A master’s degree in architecture
• Good knowledge of English and (Swiss) German: the design studios and research are mostly taught and led in English, while German is needed to work with local collaborators
• Solid knowledge of the Swiss architectural landscape, including construction, detailing, and the most common regulations
• A good understanding of architectural design practice, and of Swiss socio-economic, cultural, historical, and political context
• Residence in Switzerland, ideally in the Zurich area

Ideally, you also have
• 2-3 years of professional experience, including work on execution plans
• Knowledge of French or Italian

We offer
• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society
• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents, written in English:
• CV (max. 1 page)
• Portfolio with examples of your architectural work and research (max. 10 pages)
• Cover letter explaining your motivation and your interest in joining the Chair of Architectural Behaviorology (max. 1 page)

Further information about Department of Architecture can be found on our Website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Samuel Dayer at dayer@arch.ethz.ch (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

The application deadline is 22 November 2026.

We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

About ETH Zürich

ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.
descriptionByLocale.de:
Lehr- und Forschungsassistent (3 Positionen)

40%, Zürich, befristet

Das Departement Architektur (D-ARCH) der ETH Zürich gehört zu den weltweit führenden Architekturschulen, die für ihre Lehre ebenso bekannt sind wie für ihre Forschung. Der Lehrstuhl für Architekturverhalten unter der Leitung von Prof. Momoyo Kaijima sucht neue Mitglieder für sein Team. Folgende Positionen sind offen:
• Lehrassistent, 40%, ab Januar 2027
• Research Assistant, 40%, ab Januar 2027
• Lehrassistent, 40%, ab August 2027

Projekthintergrund

Seit 2017 untersucht der Lehrstuhl für Architekturverhalten die architektonische Form anhand von Verhaltensweisen: das Verhalten von Klima und Materialien, von Menschen und Nicht-Menschen sowie von Architekturtypologien. Dieser Ansatz zielt darauf ab, Architektur in ökologischen Netzwerken zu verstehen, eine bessere Zugänglichkeit zu Ressourcen zu schaffen und gemeinsame Commons zu finden. Wir sehen Praxis, Forschung und Bildung als eine integrierte, zyklische Aktivität, in der sich Theorie und Praxis gegenseitig informieren und gestalten.

Da Architektur an bestimmten Orten verankert ist, untersuchen wir ihre Beziehung zu regionalen Lebensstilen, einschließlich städtischer, bergiger und landwirtschaftlicher Kontexte. Dabei thematisieren wir Lücken im architektonischen Diskurs, insbesondere die Kluft zwischen Konsum- und Produktionsbereichen.

Unsere Forschungsprojekte umfassen zum Beispiel die Swiss Window Journey, eine Studie über Fenstertypologien in der Schweiz, oder die Valley Section, eine Studie über das Schweizer Industrieerbe durch territoriale Querschnitte. Wir arbeiten auch an Housing, Shelter und Care Behaviorology, die sich mit häuslichen, post-Katastrophen-und Gesundheits-Umgebungen. Gemeinsam mit anderen ETH-Lehrstühlen haben wir strukturelle und räumliche Experimente entwickelt, die auf Behaviorologie basieren.

In der Lehre leitet der Lehrstuhl ein Designstudio im zweiten Jahr, in dem rund 70 Studenten in die Methoden der Architekturverhaltenstheorie und der Akteursnetzwerktheorie eingeführt werden, als Werkzeuge sowohl für die Gestaltung von Architektur als auch für das Verständnis unseres gebauten, gelebten und sozialen Umfelds. Die Studierenden sammeln praktische Erfahrungen in der Gestaltung und Zeichnung von Architekturprojekten, Forschung, Arbeit in Teams, Bau von 1:1-Strukturen und Präsentation und Verteidigung ihrer Ideen.

Weitere Informationen über den Lehrstuhl und die Arbeit der Studierenden finden Sie auf unserer Website.

Stellenbeschreibung

Als Lehrassistent (40%) unterrichten Sie eine Kombination aus architektonischer Gestaltung und Forschung im Rahmen von Architectural Behaviorology. Sie verstehen die Ideen der Schüler und helfen ihnen, ihre Projekte weiterzuentwickeln. Mit Ihrem Wissen über Struktur, Konstruktion und Detaillierung können Sie sie auch in diesen Angelegenheiten unterstützen, und Ihr forschungsbasiertes Denken hilft ihnen, gute, praktikable Lösungen für Designprobleme zu finden. Studiotage sind dienstags und mittwochs. Ihre Aufgaben umfassen:
• Vorbereitung von Materialien und Dokumenten für das Designstudio
• Unterstützung der Studierenden bei der Entwicklung ihrer Projekte
• Bewertung und Bewertung von Studentenprojekten
• Abhalten von kurzen Input-Vorträgen und Workshops für das Studio

Als wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin (40%) forschen Sie im Rahmen von Architectural Behaviorology. Sie arbeiten an einer Vielzahl von laufenden Forschungsprojekten zu Window Behaviorology, Urban-Rural Commons, Housing in Switzerland, Architecture for Care und anderen. Unter anderem organisieren Sie Workshops und Seminarwochen, helfen bei der Bearbeitung und Veröffentlichung von Büchern und organisieren Ausstellungen.

Lehr- und Forschungsassistentenverträge sind auf ein Jahr begrenzt und können jährlich um bis zu 6 Jahre verlängert werden.

Profil

Sie haben
• Ein Master-Abschluss in Architektur
• Gute Englisch- und (Schweizer)Deutschkenntnisse: Die Designstudios und die Forschung werden hauptsächlich auf Englisch unterrichtet und geführt, während Deutsch für die Zusammenarbeit mit lokalen Mitarbeitern benötigt wird
• Fundierte Kenntnisse der Schweizer Architekturlandschaft, einschließlich Bau, Detaillierung und der gängigsten Vorschriften
• Ein gutes Verständnis der architektonischen Gestaltungspraxis und des sozioökonomischen, kulturellen, historischen und politischen Kontexts der Schweiz
• Residenz in der Schweiz, idealerweise im Raum Zürich

Idealerweise haben Sie auch
• 2-3 Jahre Berufserfahrung, einschließlich der Arbeit an Ausführungsplänen
• Kenntnisse in Französisch oder Italienisch

Wir bieten
• Ihr Job mit Impact: Werden Sie Teil der ETH Zürich, die nicht nur Ihre berufliche Entwicklung unterstützt, sondern auch aktiv zum positiven Wandel in der Gesellschaft beiträgt
• Sie können zahlreiche Vorteile erwarten, wie Saisontickets für den öffentlichen Nahverkehr und Carsharing, eine breite Palette von Sportangeboten des ASVZ, Kinderbetreuung und attraktive Pensionsleistungen.

Wir legen Wert auf Vielfalt und Nachhaltigkeit

Im Einklang mit unseren Werten fördert die ETH Zürich eine inklusive Kultur. Wir fördern Chancengleichheit, schätzen Vielfalt und fördern ein Arbeits- und Lernumfeld, in dem die Rechte und die Würde aller unserer Mitarbeiter und Studenten respektiert werden. Besuchen Sie unsere Website für Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt, um herauszufinden, wie wir ein faires und offenes Umfeld gewährleisten, in dem jeder wachsen und gedeihen kann. Nachhaltigkeit ist für uns ein zentraler Wert – wir arbeiten konsequent auf eine klimaneutrale Zukunft hin.

Neugierig? So sind wir.

Weitere Informationen zum Department of Architecture finden Sie auf unserer Website . Fragen zur Stelle richten Sie bitte an Samuel Dayer unter dayer@arch.ethz.ch (keine Bewerbungen).

Bitte beachten Sie, dass wir ausschließlich Bewerbungen annehmen, die über unser Online-Bewerbungsportal eingereicht werden. Bewerbungen per E-Mail oder Post werden nicht berücksichtigt.

Über die ETH Zürich

Die ETH Zürich ist eine der weltweit führenden Universitäten, die sich auf

descriptionByLocale.fr:
Assistant à l ' enseignement et à la recherche (3 postes)

40 %, Zurich, durée déterminée

Le Département d'Architecture (D-ARCH) de l'ETH Zurich est parmi les principales écoles d'architecture du monde, connues pour son enseignement autant que pour ses recherches. Le président de l'Architectural Behaviorology, dirigé par le professeur Momoyo Kaijima, est à la recherche de nouveaux membres pour rejoindre son équipe. Les postes suivants sont ouverts :
• Assistante pédagogique, 40%, à compter de janvier 2027
• Assistant de recherche, 40 %, à compter de janvier 2027
• Assistant pédagogique, 40%, à partir d'août 2027

Contexte du projet

Depuis 2017, la Chaire de Comportement Architectural étudie la forme architecturale à travers la lentille des comportements : le comportement du climat et des matériaux, des humains et des non-humains, et des typologies architecturales. Cette approche vise à comprendre l'architecture au sein des réseaux écologiques, à améliorer l'accessibilité aux ressources et à trouver des biens communs communs. Nous considérons la pratique, la recherche et l'éducation comme une activité cyclique intégrée dans laquelle la théorie et la pratique s'informent et se façonnent.

Parce que l'architecture est ancrée dans des endroits précis, nous explorons sa relation avec les modes de vie régionaux, y compris les contextes urbains, montagneux et agricoles. Ce faisant, nous nous attaquons aux lacunes du discours architectural, en particulier au fossé entre les domaines de la consommation et de la production.

Nos projets de recherche comprennent, par exemple, Swiss Window Journey , une étude des typologies des fenêtres à travers la Suisse, ou Valley Section , une étude du patrimoine industriel suisse à travers des sections territoriales. Nous travaillons également sur le logement, le logement et la comportement des soins, qui traitent des environnements domestiques, post-catastrophes et de soins de santé. Avec d'autres chaises ETH, nous avons développé des expériences structurales et spatiales enracinées dans le comportement.

Dans l'enseignement, la chaire dirige un studio de design de deuxième année, où environ 70 étudiants sont initiés aux méthodologies de l'architecture comportementale et de la théorie du réseau d'acteurs, comme outils à la fois pour concevoir l'architecture et pour comprendre notre environnement bâti, vécu et social. Les étudiants acquièrent une expérience pratique dans la conception et le dessin de projets d'architecture, la recherche, le travail en équipe, la construction de structures 1:1, la présentation et la défense de leurs idées.

Vous pouvez trouver plus d'informations sur la chaise et le travail des étudiants sur notre site .

Description du poste

En tant qu'assistant d'enseignement (40%), vous enseignez une combinaison de conception architecturale et de recherche dans le cadre de l'architecture comportementale. Vous comprenez les idées des étudiants et les aidez à développer leurs projets. Votre connaissance de la structure, de la construction et du détail vous permet également de les soutenir dans ces domaines, et votre réflexion basée sur la recherche les aide à trouver des solutions efficaces et réalisables aux problèmes de conception. Les journées studio sont le mardi et le mercredi. Vos tâches comprennent :
• Préparation des matériaux et documents pour le studio de design
• Aider les étudiants à développer leurs projets
• Évaluation et classement des projets étudiants
• Organisation de brèves conférences et ateliers pour le studio

En tant qu'assistant de recherche (40 %), vous effectuez des recherches dans le cadre de l'architecture comportementale. Vous travaillez sur un large éventail de projets de recherche en cours sur le comportement des fenêtres, Urban-Rural Commons, Logement en Suisse, Architecture for Care, etc. Entre autres tâches, vous organisez des ateliers et des semaines de séminaire, aidez à éditer et publier des livres et organisez des expositions.

Les contrats d'assistants à l'enseignement et à la recherche sont limités à un an et peuvent être renouvelés chaque année pour une durée maximale de six ans.

Profil

Vous avez
• Maîtrise en architecture
• Bonne connaissance de l'anglais et de l'allemand (suisse): les studios de design et la recherche sont principalement enseignés et dirigés en anglais, tandis que l'allemand est nécessaire pour travailler avec des collaborateurs locaux
• Bonne connaissance du paysage architectural suisse, y compris la construction, le détail et les règlements les plus courants
• Une bonne compréhension de la pratique du design architectural et du contexte socio-économique, culturel, historique et politique suisse
• Résidence en Suisse, idéalement dans la région de Zurich

Idéalement, vous avez aussi
• 2-3 ans d'expérience professionnelle, y compris sur les plans d'exécution
• Connaissance du français ou de l'italien

Nous offrons
• Votre travail avec impact: Devenez membre de l'ETH Zurich, qui non seulement soutient votre développement professionnel, mais contribue également activement au changement positif dans la société
• Vous pouvez vous attendre à de nombreux avantages , tels que les billets de saison de transport en commun et le partage de voiture , un large éventail de sports offerts par l'ASVZ , garde d'enfants et prestations de retraite attrayantes

Nous apprécions la diversité et la durabilité

Conformément à nos valeurs, ETH Zurich encourage une culture inclusive. Nous favorisons l'égalité des chances, valorisons la diversité et favorisons un environnement de travail et d'apprentissage dans lequel les droits et la dignité de tous nos employés et étudiants sont respectés. Visitez notre site Web sur l'égalité des chances et la diversité pour découvrir comment nous garantissons un environnement équitable et ouvert qui permet à tous de grandir et de prospérer. La durabilité est une valeur fondamentale pour nous – nous travaillons constamment vers un avenir neutre sur le plan climatique.

Curieux ? Nous aussi.

Nous sommes impatients de recevoir votre candidature en ligne avec les documents suivants, rédigés en anglais:
• CV (max. 1 page)
• Portfolio avec des exemples de vos travaux d'architecture et de recherche (max. 10 pages)
• Lettre d'accompagnement expliquant votre motivation et votre intérêt à rejoindre la Chaire de comportement architectural (max. 1 page)

De plus amples informations sur le Département d'Architecture sont disponibles sur notre site web . Les questions concernant le poste doivent être adressées à Samuel Dayer à dayer@arch.ethz.ch (aucune demande).

Veuillez noter que nous acceptons exclusivement les demandes soumises par notre portail en ligne. Les demandes par courriel ou par la poste ne seront pas prises en considération.

La date limite de présentation des demandes est le 22 novembre 2026.

Nous tenons à souligner que la présélection est effectuée par les recruteurs responsables et non par l'intelligence artificielle.

À propos d'ETH Zürich

ETH Zurich est l'une des principales universités du monde spécialisées dans
science et technologie. Nous sommes réputés pour notre excellente éducation,
recherche fondamentale de pointe et transfert direct de nouvelles connaissances
dans la société. Plus de 30 000 personnes de plus de 120 pays trouvent notre
l'université d'être un lieu qui favorise la pensée indépendante et un
un environnement qui inspire l'excellence. Situé au cœur de l'Europe,

jobs.description:
Doctoral Student in Quantum Error Correction

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

We invite applications for a doctoral position in the theory of quantum error correction at ETH Zurich, supervised by Joseph M. Renes and co-supervised by Renato Renner.

Quantum computers promise capabilities far beyond today's computers, but only if we can reliably protect quantum information from errors. Quantum error correction (QEC) is therefore one of the central challenges on the path toward large-scale quantum computing. In this Doctoral project, you will investigate the fundamental limits of quantum error correction.

The position is part of QuBriC , the first European Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network (MSCDN) dedicated entirely to QEC, and includes secondments to Politecnico di Milano and Quantinuum in Cambridge, England. The PhD position is fully funded for 3 years.

The expected starting date is early/mid 2027, but a later start is also possible.

Job description
• Your main responsibility will be to conduct high-quality research within the project and progressively develop your own research ideas
• The exact direction of the project can be shaped according to your background and research interests
• You will perform numerical experiments and theoretical analysis, develop algorithms and software, and communicate your results through publications and presentations at leading international conferences and journals
• You will collaborate extensively with researchers within QuBriC and participate in the network's research, training, and dissemination activities.
• The position also includes teaching at the undergraduate and Master's level and other departmental duties, corresponding to up to 20% full time
• The position is a fixed-term appointment of three years, with a starting salary of 61’400.00 CHF per annum.

Profile

To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree (or equivalent) in physics, mathematics, electrical engineering, computer science, or a closely related field.

The following will strengthen your application:
• A strong mathematical background, with roots in either information theory or quantum information science
• Curiosity about the implications of quantum mechanics for information processing
• Motivation to deliver ambitious, high-quality work
• Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in an international research environment
• Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
• Strong programming skills (e.g., Python, Matlab, or similar)
• Familiarity with classical and/or quantum coding theory, error correcting codes, and decoding algorithms
• Previous experience in research and teaching

Quantum computers promise capabilities far beyond today's computers, but only if we can reliably protect quantum information from errors. Quantum error correction (QEC) is therefore one of the central challenges on the path toward large-scale quantum computing. In this Doctoral project, you will investigate the fundamental limits of quantum error correction.

Quantencomputer versprechen Fähigkeiten, die weit über die heutigen Computer hinausgehen, aber nur, wenn wir Quanteninformationen zuverlässig vor Fehlern schützen können. Die Quantenfehlerkorrektur (QEC) ist daher eine der zentralen Herausforderungen auf dem Weg zum Quantencomputing im großen Maßstab. In diesem Doktorandenprojekt werden Sie die grundlegenden Grenzen der Quantenfehlerkorrektur untersuchen.

To strengthen our team, we are looking for a dedicated employee who is enthusiastic about this specialized and responsible task.

Job description

In addition to the acceptance, cleaning and disinfection of the goods to be sterilized, her responsibilities include logistics and communication with researchers and animal keepers within the SPF barrier.

Profile
• Open-minded, resilient and communicative personality who enjoys working in a team in a lively, international university environment
• High willingness to take responsibility, resilience and reliability
• Good knowledge of German and English for capturing, understanding, following and implementing hazard statements and operating instructions
• Readiness to operate large electronic devices reliably and appropriately
• Good physical constitution since it is physical, mainly standing and walking activities
• Working under personal protective clothing such as laboratory clothing, mouth mask, vinyl gloves

• Independence and flexibility round off your profile

We offer
• Interesting and varied work at one of the most renowned universities in the world
• A comprehensive and structured familiarization by experienced and qualified colleagues:
• An appreciative, collaborative working environment and participation in a committed, open-minded and multicultural team
• Attractive employment conditions and social benefits according to the guidelines of ETH Zurich
• Attractive pension services through the PUBLICA pension scheme

Diversity and sustainability are important to us

In line with our values, ETH Zurich supports an inclusive culture. We promote equal opportunities, value diversity and foster a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all employees and students are respected. On our website on equal opportunities and diversity, you will learn how we ensure a fair and open environment in which everyone can develop and flourish. Sustainability is a key value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future.

Curious? We are too.

We look forward to your online application with the following documents:
• Letter of motivation
• CVC
• Diplomas
• Employment certificates

More information about the ETH Phenomics Center can be found on our website. For further information, Mr. Carlos Mateus Jorge, head of the sink kitchen, cjorge@ethz.ch (no application documents), is at your disposal.

Please apply exclusively via the online application portal. Applications by e-mail or by post will not be considered.

We are happy to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

In order to protect the health of our employees and animals as well as to ensure the health suitability for the intended activity, a medical examination is carried out by our occupational doctor in the event of possible employment. For recruitment agencies, the terms and conditions of ETH Zurich apply.

About ETH Zurich

ETH Zurich is one of the best technical science universities in the world. We are known for our excellent teaching, groundbreaking basic research and the direct transfer of new findings into society. More than 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find an environment that promotes independent thinking and a climate that inspires excellence. At the heart of Europe and globally networked, we jointly develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

jobs.description:
Senior Analog/Mixed-Signal IC Design Specialist

100%, Zurich, permanent

The Microelectronics Design Center (DZ) of the Department of Information Technologies and Electrical Engineering (D-ITET) is a technical support group providing design tools, know-how and licenses for ASIC, FPGA, Embedded Systems and PCB design for research and teaching . This includes consulting, project planning, reviewing of active projects as well as participation in projects. To lead the area of Analog/Mixed-Signal IC Design we are seeking a Senior Analog/Mixed-Signal IC Design Specialist starting 1st of January 2027 or by mutual agreement.

Job description
• You will be part of an experienced team and be the expert for analog/mixed-signal in the DZ.
• You will own the analog/mixed-signal area of the IC design infrastructure and further develop it with the aim to provide support to researchers and students.
• You will support design flows covering all aspects of IC design with a strong focus on analog/mixed-signal design flows using the latest tools from Cadence Design System, Synopsys, Mentor Graphics and open-source tools.
• You will interact with students and researchers to help them with their IC design related questions, chip finishing and submission of ICs to fabrication through MPW and foundry contacts.
• You will also be asked to develop, adapt and maintain common building blocks for mixed-signal IC chips as well as the development of larger mixed-signal ICs.
• As part of a team supporting research and teaching at ETH Zurich, you will frequently be challenged to develop solutions for systems that stretch the boundaries of conventional approaches.
• You will be asked to help researchers and students through design reviews.
• You will also develop and deliver targeted training modules and hands-on laboratory sessions for students and researchers in these areas.
• In addition, you will contribute to the group's outreach and visibility by supporting its web presence and preparing periodic activity reports.

Profile

We are looking for an experienced IC designer with strong expertise in analog/mixed-signal design, motivated to work in an environment where creative technical problem-solving supports researchers and students. Given the level and breadth of the technical challenges involved, a PhD in Electrical or Computer Engineering is preferred. Candidates should bring at least 5 years of IC design experience, gained in industry or at a qualified research institution, including hands-on familiarity with tape-out procedures. A track record of multiple successful analog/mixed-signal tape-outs across a range of technology nodes, including advanced ones such as 22nm and FinFET, is required, as is experience leading chip tape-out projects. Proficiency with UNIX, scripting languages, and IC design tools from major EDA vendors is also required. Good written and spoken English is essential for technical collaboration in a multicultural environment. Experience organizing technical training courses and undergraduate laboratory activities is highly desirable. The ideal candidate combines strong communication and technical skills, with the ability to engage both technical and non-technical audiences and is comfortable taking on a leading and senior technical role within the team.

We offer

We are a small support team of four permanent employees, and are looking forward to add a fifth member to the team. As a support group we expect you to be present mostly in the office to interact with students and research staff, however we can accommodate some home office hours per week as long as it aligns with the rest of the group.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity in our team. We are most interested in finding the best candidate for the job and that candidate may be one who comes from a less traditional background. If you are interested in this role but your past experience does not align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply.

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:
• A letter of motivation
• CV
• Diplomas
• Certificates of employment

The application deadline is 30 November 2026 .

Further information about Microelectronics Design Center can be found on our Website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Frank K. Gürkaynak, +41 44 632 2726 or kgf@iis.ee.ethz.ch (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

For recruitment services the GTC of ETH Zurich apply.

About ETH Zürich

ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.
